Fission 于 2024 年成立，创始团队包括 Point72 和 Securitize 前员工。目前客户主要为机构投资者及持有链上资产的组织，包括持有代币化私募信贷或股权资产的对冲基金、管理财库的加密机构，以及将储备配置于生息代币化投资产品的稳定币发行商。

items.content:
HTX DeepThink：CPI冲击后杠杆仍在累积，加密市场去杠杆风险上升

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 15 日，HTX DeepThink 专栏作者、HTX Research 研究员 Chloe 分析指出，美国 9 月 CPI 带来的冲击已从利率预期调整扩散至整体风险偏好，而衍生品市场的去杠杆尚未完成，加密市场短期仍面临下行压力。数据公布后，美债收益率一度快速上行，随后涨幅部分回落，加密市场跌势却仍在延续，截至北京时间 10 月 15 日 12:00，BTC 累计下跌 3.50%，ETH 下跌 6.27%。

从历史数据看，CPI 对加密市场的冲击主要集中在短期。过去 18 次 CPI 发布中，通胀超预期幅度与发布后 30 分钟内 BTC 收益的相关系数为 -0.46，到 4 小时和 24 小时分别降至 -0.14 和 -0.09。宏观数据给出初始方向，后续走势更多取决于流动性、机构资金与杠杆结构。本次数据发布后 30 分钟内，BTC 成交额放大约 5 倍，83,000 美元附近的初始承接仍未能阻止下跌；BTC 现货 ETF 近六个交易日累计净流出约 8.59 亿美元，现货支撑进一步削弱。

衍生品数据同样显示杠杆尚未出清。CPI 发布后 4 小时内，主要币种未平仓合约普遍增加，其中，截至次日中午 SOL 未平仓合约增长 7.95%，说明下跌过程中杠杆风险仍在积累。

未来 1 至 3 天，市场整体或维持谨慎偏空。BTC 可能受空头回补推动反弹至 81,600 美元附近，但在美元强势、ETF 资金流出与核心通胀压力未缓解的背景下，仍有重新测试 80,200 美元的风险；若跌破该位置并伴随未平仓合约快速下降，可能触发进一步去杠杆。83,860 美元是判断本轮 CPI 冲击是否被充分消化的重要参考位置，短期内山寨币的下行弹性预计继续高于 BTC。

注：本文内容并非投资意见，亦不构成任何投资产品之要约、要约招揽或建议。

items.author: Cointelegraph by Zoltan Vardai
items.content:
White House crypto council chief Patrick Witt steps down
Witt’s departure leaves a leadership gap at the White House Crypto Council and marks the fourth high-profile exit from the advisory group.
Patrick Witt, the executive director of the White House’s Crypto Council, is leaving his current role for a new opportunity in the private sector.
“Serving in this administration has been the privilege of a lifetime,” wrote Witt in a Thursday X post, adding that he looks forward to continuing to support US technological advancements “in the private sector.”
Witt served as the White House’s leading advisor on the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, would have created the first comprehensive US regulatory framework for the crypto market. The US Senate failed to pass a cloture motion on the legislation in September and further progress this session is unlikely.
Witt’s exit leaves a leadership gap as he was the last remaining staffer on the White House’s council, following the March departure of White House crypto and AI czar, David Sacks and the July departure of deputy director Harry Jung.
The council’s former executive director, Bo Hines, announced his departure in August 2025. Weeks later, Hines took a role as a strategic adviser at stablecoin issuer Tether, to coordinate the company’s US expansion.
Cointelegraph has approached the White House for comment on Witt’s departure and whether they have a potential replacement to fill his role and will update when available.
Related: Patrick Witt defers military training as CLARITY heads to Senate

items.author: Cointelegraph by Ezra Reguerra
items.content:
Starknet opens vote on potential Ethereum L2 exit over quantum risks
Starknet is asking STRK holders whether to explore becoming an independent layer-1 blockchain to reduce its dependence on Ethereum’s quantum-security upgrade timeline.
Ethereum layer-2 network Starknet has opened a non-binding vote asking STRK holders whether it should explore becoming an independent, post-quantum layer-1 blockchain.
On Thursday, Starknet opened a seven-day poll, which offers three options: support further research, oppose it, or remain neutral pending more information. Voting closes on Oct. 22, with results published afterwards.
A “Yes” vote would signal support for further research, not authorize a transition. Further proposals and governance votes would be required, and no timetable for becoming an L1 has been announced.
StarkWare, the developer behind Starknet, said the move could allow the network to pursue quantum-resistant security without depending on Ethereum’s upgrade schedule. Starknet currently relies on Ethereum for infrastructure, including its bridge and data availability, which StarkWare identifies as remaining quantum-security dependencies.
“Quantum-proofing crypto is urgent, so we must move at lightning speed,” StarkWare CEO Eli Ben-Sasson told Cointelegraph, contrasting the proposal with what he described as slower progress at Ethereum and Bitcoin.
Both Ben-Sasson and Starknet hinted at the proposal in separate X posts on Oct. 8, framing it as a move to become “the first fully quantum-resistant network” by 2027.
In June, StarkWare unveiled a three-phase quantum-resistance roadmap for Starknet, covering signature upgrades, smart-contract migration and Ethereum-dependent infrastructure.
In March, Ethereum developers established a dedicated post-quantum team, aiming to introduce initial protocol-level protections by 2029.
Related: Starknet introduces wallet privacy feature for DeFi activity

items.content:
Anthropic给Claude API加上运行追踪：Agent卡在哪、Token烧在哪都能查

动察 Beating AI 快讯，Anthropic 开放 Claude Platform 的 OpenTelemetry 追踪功能公测。一个 Agent 连续调用模型、搜索资料、执行工具，开发者现在可以沿着运行记录，查看每次调用花了多久、哪里出了错、消耗了多少 Token。不用再从不同服务的日志里拼凑执行过程，就能找到拖慢任务或增加成本的环节。

这次最重要的变化是 API 原生支持。Claude Code 和 Cowork 此前已有类似监控能力，现在 Messages API 和云端托管 Agent 也能直接把运行记录发送到 Grafana、Datadog、Langfuse 等平台。管理员只需在 Claude Console 配置接收地址，不必逐个修改现有 API 调用。不过，开发者自己运行的工具仍需通过 SDK 等方式补充追踪记录。

items.ai_summary: Brooklyn prosecutors and the FBI disrupted 112 servers and 241 web domains tied to a multinational crypto investment scam that targeted Russian-speaking Americans and stole tens of millions of dollars, seizing about $300,000 in stolen funds so far.
items.author: Decrypt Agent
items.content:
In brief
- The Brooklyn District Attorney's Virtual Currency Unit, working with the FBI, disrupted 112 servers and 241 web domains used in a crypto investment scam.
- The operation targeted Russian-speaking Americans through Facebook ads, and prosecutors estimate it stole tens of millions of dollars, some of it victims' entire life savings.
- Prosecutors have seized about $300,000 in stolen funds so far and say they are working to recover more.
Brooklyn prosecutors have dismantled the online infrastructure of a multinational crypto investment scam that targeted Russian speakers in the U.S., seizing and disrupting 241 web domains and 112 servers, District Attorney Eric Gonzalez announced on Wednesday.
The office's Virtual Currency Unit carried out search warrants and other enforcement actions across three time zones last week, working with the FBI. The servers were hosted by Eastern European and American companies, and the scammers relied on infrastructure and IP addresses in Ukraine and other Eastern European countries, according to the release.
"These criminals stole many millions of dollars from Russian-speaking victims through an elaborate investment scheme, then tried to exploit them again with false promises to recover their money," Gonzalez said.
A large cluster of victims in Brooklyn had each responded to a Russian-language Facebook ad for investment opportunities and then received a call from an "investment advisor" who coached them into opening an account on a crypto investment website, the office said.
With the advisor's help, victims bought crypto and sent it to addresses linked to the platforms. When they tried to withdraw after weeks or months of "investing," they were locked out or told to pay additional fees and taxes.
Data from the seized servers showed the scammers also ran a recovery scam, contacting victims a few weeks after the initial fraud and promising to get their stolen assets back, the DA's office said.
Brooklyn's Virtual Currency Unit
The unit had been investigating the operation for three years. Brooklyn's large Russian-speaking population meant the scam hit the borough's residents disproportionately, according to the release.
Before last week, the unit had already seized or disrupted 400 domains linked to the fraud, but new scam websites kept appearing. Taking down the servers removes the scammers' ability to quickly create new sites and contact existing victims, the office said.
Prosecutors estimate that tens of millions of dollars were stolen in the scheme. The office has seized about $300,000 so far and is working to claw back more.
The takedown is not the Brooklyn DA's only recent crypto fraud case. Its prosecutors previously charged a local man who stole $16 million from nearly 100 Coinbase users through a phishing scheme. He was sentenced to up to 12 years in prison.

Hyperliquid founder wants U.S. oversight of trading platforms, not his blockchain
Jeff Yan told Bloomberg that U.S. regulatory oversight should apply to the firms using the blockchain, not to the underlying network itself.
- Hyperliquid founder Jeff Yan said U.S. regulators should oversee financial firms operating on the blockchain rather than regulate the network itself.
- Yan’s proposal could allow Wall Street firms to build regulated trading businesses on Hyperliquid without requiring the blockchain to register as an exchange.
- Kraken parent Payward plans to offer U.S. investors derivatives using Hyperliquid’s technology through a regulated exchange, even as Hyperliquid’s perpetual futures market remains closed to them.
Hyperliquid founder Jeff Yan wants U.S. regulators to oversee financial firms using his blockchain rather than the network itself.
Companies operating trading markets on Hyperliquid should be responsible for meeting regulatory requirements, much like financial firms using internet infrastructure, Yan said Thursday in a Bloomberg interview.
“The regulation sits at the layer where there are controls, and indeed the deployers are the ones that exercise these controls,” Yan said.
Hyperliquid, best known for its eponymous perpetual futures trading platform, remains closed to U.S. customers.
However, Kraken’s parent company, Payward, plans to offer investors in the country derivatives using Hyperliquid’s technology through a regulated exchange. For Hyperliquid, this means it could add a Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) regulated operator even though its perps market remains unavailable to U.S. customers.
Yan’s proposal would allow Wall Street firms to build trading businesses on Hyperliquid without requiring the blockchain itself to operate as a regulated exchange.
“We’re not trying to displace anything,” Yan said. “In fact, I think the technology can benefit everyone who currently operates markets in a more traditional setting.”
His comments come after President Donald Trump said in August that the CFTC was working to bring Hyperliquid into the U.S. under federal regulations.

items.author: Cointelegraph by Zoltan Vardai
items.content:
Bitget, Liquid exploits push Q3 crypto hacks toward $1.2B
Compromised suppliers, developer tools and infrastructure components outside security audits drove about 77% of the quarter’s total losses, according to Hacken.
Cryptocurrency hacks soared to $1.18 billion across 107 recorded incidents in the third quarter of 2026, according to security company Hacken.
Hacken’s Q3 report attributed 77% (about $906 million) to compromised suppliers or developer tools, publicly disclosed fixes that had not been deployed, or other components outside security reviews.
The four largest incidents included the $387 million Bitget hack, the $320 million Liquid Network exploit, the $120 million Tectonic exploit, and the Coldcard firmware vulnerability, associated with an estimated $115 million in losses.
This Q3 was the most damaging quarter for crypto hacks since Q1 2025, when Bybit’s $1.4 billion loss to North Korea pushed the total to $1.6 billion.
Q3 losses in total amount and composition. Source: Hacken
About 80% of the quarter’s losses were concentrated in four of the largest incidents, while 98 of the incidents recorded losses below $10 million. The median loss across all 107 incidents was $670,000.
While supplier compromises and infrastructure failures drove much of the stolen value, smart contract incidents were the most frequent, accounting for $228 million in losses across 71 incidents as the most exploited attack vector.
Related: Anthropic warns ‘AI worms’ may autonomously spread across devices like a virus
About a third of losses was returned or reversed after Q3 crypto hacks
Of the $1.18 billion lost, about $387 million was returned or reversed, accounting for the recovery of about 33% of gross losses.
Following the Liquid Network hack, self-proclaimed “white hats” returned $272 million, representing about 85% of the stolen value.
In the Tectonic incident, Cronos validators rolled back 114 minutes of settled blockchain history, reversing about $111.2 million of the $120.4 million in affected borrowing. Also, stablecoin issuers Circle and Tether froze about $340,000 tied to the Bitget theft.
Operators covered an additional $410 million of user losses from their own funds. Bitget’s user protection fund covered $387 million, while Triple-A, Coinsbuy and TAC repaid about $22 million, making users whole, while stolen assets remained with attackers.
About $384 million, or 32% of gross losses, was neither returned nor covered.
Amount of losses covered by operators, compared to amount returned or reversed. Source: Hacken
Hacken urged industry participants to strengthen the cybersecurity of third-party suppliers, developer tools and other external infrastructure that may fall outside security audits.
The company also recommended that protocols expand security audits to include oracles, bridgers, custody systems, signing authorities and other privileged components.

items.author: Olivier Acuna
items.content:
Australia’s financial watchdog seeks stiffer rules for crypto exchanges ahead of licensing deadline
The country’s regulator, ASIC, has proposed tougher rules to protect users’ digital assets, crypto trading and to safeguard the country’s financial stability.
- Australia’s financial regulator proposed standards requiring cryptocurrency exchanges and digital asset custodians to safeguard customer funds, ensure transparent trading and meet financial requirements.
- The rules take effect April 8, 2027, and existing firms may continue operating if they apply for a license by Oct. 7, 2027, while regulators review their applications.
- The consultation closes Nov. 27, with final guidance expected in March 2027, as Australia moves to regulate crypto businesses more like traditional financial firms.
Australia's financial regulator proposed new standards for cryptocurrency exchanges and digital asset custodians, setting out how companies must protect customer funds, execute trades and meet financial requirements under laws that take effect next year.
The Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) said it opened a consultation on the rules on Thursday, which would require affected firms to obtain or update their regulatory approval or license. The consultation closes on Nov. 27, with final guidance and standards expected in March 2027.
The proposals mark the next step in Australia’s effort to bring crypto businesses under the same regulatory framework as traditional financial firms. Parliament passed the legislation in April, joining jurisdictions such as the European Union, Singapore and Hong Kong, which have introduced dedicated crypto regulations.
Australia's move comes years after the 2022 collapse of FTX left about 30,000 Australian customers unable to access their money. Three years earlier, Cryptopia, an exchange in neighboring New Zealand, went bankrupt after a major hack.
The rules take effect on April 8, 2027. Crypto firms already operating in the country have until Oct. 7 of the next year to apply for a license and can continue doing business while ASIC reviews their applications.
For Australian investors, the changes would mean clearer rules on how exchanges hold their assets, execute orders and handle conflicts of interest. Crypto companies would face new compliance obligations and financial requirements to operate legally in the country.
"Our approach is based on the principle of 'same activity, same risk, same regulatory outcome' to align Australia with the approach of comparable overseas jurisdictions," ASIC Commissioner Alan Kirkland said.
Under the consultation paper, platforms would be subject to standards covering the separation and safeguarding of customer assets, trading transparency, settlement procedures and financial resources. The proposed trading rules also address market manipulation, conflicts of interest and how exchanges handle customer orders.
ASIC said it has recorded more than 140 applications from businesses seeking authorization to provide digital asset-related financial services. It also said stablecoins used for payments are being addressed separately through Australia's payment services reforms.

items.author: Cointelegraph by William Suberg
items.content:
Bitcoin dips to $80.1K as KOSPI closes at its lowest since April
Bitcoin price action continued to see contagion from a Korean tech sell-off after the KOSPI Index fell 7.5% on Thursday.
Bitcoin (BTC) fell to its lowest levels in over three weeks on Thursday as crypto tracked fresh losses on South Korean stock markets.
Key points:
- Bitcoin reached new local lows of $80,154 as downside pressure returned to South Korean equities.
- The KOSPI closed Thursday at 5,554 points, its lowest since early April, driven by a rout in tech stocks.
- Oil prices cooled, with Brent crude dropping more than 2% despite an “unjustifiable” Singapore fuel-tanker strike in the Strait of Hormuz.
Bitcoin price nears $80,000 as KOSPI falls 7.5%
Data from TradingView showed BTC/USD hitting $80,154 on Bitstamp, a level last seen on Sept. 20.
BTC/USD one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
The weakness came after South Korea’s Korea Composite Stock Price Index, or KOSPI, finished the day 7.5% lower, taking week-to-date losses to 15.5%.
KOSPI Composite Index one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
As with earlier in the week, tech giants bore the brunt of the sell-off, with SK Hynix down 11% and Samsung Electronics finishing 9.5% lower on the day.
SK Hynix stock one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
As Cointelegraph reported, concerns over AI debt obligations, foreign capital outflows and competition from China contributed to the South Korean market rout, with KOSPI’s 200-day moving average dropping to as low as 5,450 points, a level not seen since late July. It ended Thursday’s trading session at 5,554 points, marking its lowest daily close since April 8.
Talking to local media publication The Korea Herald, Mirae Asset Securities analyst Kim Seok-hwan warned that global macro headwinds would add further friction going forward.
“Volatility is expected to persist in the near term,” he said. “As domestic supply-demand conditions deteriorate, the market has become more sensitive to external risks, while a near-term improvement in the global environment appears unlikely.”
SK Hynix and Samsung will release third-quarter earnings data on Oct. 28 and 29, respectively, potentially adding to downside volatility in investor tech sentiment should the numbers fall short of projections. Samsung is expected to confirm Q3 sales of 195 trillion won ($145 billion) and an operating profit of around 107 trillion won ($80 billion).
Oil falls despite Singapore tanker sinking
Downside pressure on Bitcoin was compounded on the back of Wednesday’s higher-than-expected US inflation data.
The September print of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) came in at 3.7% year-on-year, sparking a hawkish shift in market expectations of further interest-rate hikes by the Federal Reserve.
“Does the beat force further hiking — or does credit stress prompt policy recalibration?” trading company QCP Capital asked alongside its macro analysis seen by Cointelegraph on Thursday.
Related: CryptoQuant’s 3 charts keeping Bitcoin’s ‘Uptober’ thesis valid
With high oil prices accounting for a significant portion of the uptick in CPI, both WTI and Brent crude fell on Thursday despite mounting tensions in the Middle East. A Singapore-registered oil tanker was sunk in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, a move that the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore described as “unjustifiable.”
Speaking to CNBC, Firas Bechwaty, head of business development at online trading platform ICM, saw little chance of Hormuz transit volumes returning to levels from before the US-Iran war began.
“At the same time, Saudi crude continues to reach international buyers through alternative routes, while accelerated emergency stock releases by IEA members provide an additional buffer, preventing a sharp rise in prices, even as tensions remain elevated,” he observed.
At the time of writing, WTI traded below $95 per barrel, down 0.5%, while Brent was 2.2% lower at $103.7 per barrel.
CFDs on Brent crude oil one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
items.title: Bitcoin dips to $80.1K as KOSPI closes at its lowest since April

高油价或持续至2028年，市场担忧战争结束也难以缓解能源压力

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 15 日，路透社专栏作者罗恩·布索（Ron Bousso）撰文，伊朗战争持续时间超出市场预期，原油交易员正重新评估全球能源市场前景，预计高油价可能延续至 2028 年。布伦特原油 2027 年 12 月交割合约自 9 月初以来上涨逾 13%，至每桶 86 美元，创该合约上市以来新高；2026 年 12 月合约同期上涨约 12%。

远期油价走高与国际能源署（IEA）预计 2027 年全球石油供应增加、市场出现明显过剩的判断形成反差，反映交易员对供应能否如期恢复存在疑虑。尽管近期通过霍尔木兹海峡的石油流量已接近战前水平，但伊朗袭击船只、胡塞武装加大对沙特的袭击，以及炼油产能受损等风险，仍令供应前景承压。

柴油市场的紧张局势尤为突出。欧洲基准柴油期货 9 月中旬一度升至每吨 1480 美元的历史高位，2027 年 12 月交割合约本周首次突破每吨 1000 美元，远高于战争爆发前的 644 美元。

布索指出，即使战事结束，受损炼油设施修复、库存回补和物流体系重建仍需时间，运输、保险及军事护航等额外成本也可能持续存在，令能源成本压力延续至更长时间。

items.author: Cointelegraph by Helen Partz
items.content:
Thailand crypto ETFs may see slow start despite new rules: CoinShares
Thailand’s new Bitcoin and Ether ETF rules take effect Friday, but CoinShares expects modest initial inflows as existing investment options compete for demand.
Thailand’s first crypto exchange-traded funds (ETFs) may get off to a slow start despite Bangkok’s efforts to expand access to regulated digital asset investments.
“I would expect modest inflows initially, with tens of millions of US dollars across the first products a more realistic starting expectation than billions,” James Butterfill, head of research at digital asset investment firm CoinShares, told Cointelegraph.
The country opens a new route for crypto exposure on Friday as its rules for Bitcoin (BTC) and Ether (ETH) ETFs to list on the Stock Exchange of Thailand take effect.
The rules will allow retail Thai investors to access locally listed crypto ETFs, while restricting overseas crypto ETF investments through domestic brokers to institutional and ultra-high-net-worth investors.
Thailand’s first crypto funds will need regulatory approval and the necessary custody and distribution arrangements before trading can begin.
Hong Kong offers a cautionary comparison
Butterfill pointed to Hong Kong as an example of how even a major financial center can struggle to attract substantial crypto ETF inflows.
Hong Kong accounts for just 0.42% of assets in global crypto exchange-traded products (ETPs) despite the city’s status as an international financial hub, he said.
Global crypto investment products held $172.9 billion in assets under management, including $733 million in Hong Kong, according to CoinShares data as of late September.
First Thai crypto ETF launches remain uncertain
Butterfill said that existing investment options may limit demand for new Thai ETFs, as some investors already gain Bitcoin exposure through foreign funds or direct crypto trading.
Thailand’s MFC Asset Management, which Butterfill identified as a firm worth watching for potential ETF launches, introduced its Bitcoin ETF Tracker Fund (MBTCETF-UI) in 2024. The fund invests in BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT), the world’s largest spot Bitcoin ETF by assets under management.
“Local ETFs therefore need to attract new investors or offer a compelling reason to switch,” Butterfill said.
Apart from MFC, Butterfill pointed to ONE Asset Management as another potential ETF issuer worth watching. In 2024, ONE became the first Thai asset manager to receive approval for a Bitcoin ETF-linked fund.
Related: Bitcoin ETFs shed $261M as XRP funds buck weekly outflow trend
Butterfill said he hadn’t confirmed either company’s plans to launch a locally listed crypto ETF or when the first products might begin trading.
Cointelegraph contacted Thailand’s SEC, ONE Asset Management and MFC Asset Management about potential ETF launches but had not received responses by publication time.
Magazine: China’s P2P stablecoin wallets surge 43x, Korea’s $450B crypto economy: Asia Express
items.title: Thailand crypto ETFs may see slow start despite new rules: CoinShares

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 15 日，美国 9 月生产者价格指数（PPI）将于北京时间 10 月 15 日 20:30 公布。美国 8 月柴油价格环比上涨 24%、同比上涨 77%，美国汽车协会数据显示，柴油零售价格 9 月 22 日一度升至每加仑 6.528 美元，创历史新高，截至周三仍达 6.30 美元，较去年同期上涨逾 70%。牛津经济研究院预计，美国 9 月 PPI 环比将上涨 0.6%，高于市场预期的 0.5% 及 8 月的 0.4%。

分析人士指出，柴油是公路货运、铁路运输和农业生产的重要投入，其价格上涨会先推高企业生产与运输成本，再通过燃油附加费、运输合同和零售定价逐步传导至消费者。即使柴油价格停止上涨，成本转嫁仍可能存在滞后，意味着通胀压力尚未完全显现。

特朗普政府已采取措施缓解燃料供应压力，包括暂时放宽部分农业燃料使用限制，并称俄罗斯将向全球市场供应柴油。但业内人士认为，这些措施难以在短期内解决炼油产能和成品油供应瓶颈。市场将关注本次 PPI 能否进一步印证能源成本冲击正向企业端价格扩散。

items.author: Cointelegraph by Ezra Reguerra
items.content:
Babylon advances native Bitcoin lending proposal on Aave V4
Babylon’s proposal to bring native Bitcoin collateral to Aave V4 has entered a new governance stage, but further votes and security reviews remain before launch.
Bitcoin-focused developer Babylon Labs has submitted a proposal to let users borrow stablecoins on Aave against native Bitcoin (BTC).
Under the hood, users would lock their BTC in vaults on the Bitcoin network and borrow against it on Aave. A non-transferable token on Ethereum would represent the collateral, while the BTC itself would remain on its native blockchain without being bridged or wrapped.
The Wednesday proposal follows an initial submission on May 25 and a preliminary community vote that passed on June 10, according to Babylon Labs.
Under the proposal, Aave DAO would receive the first $500,000 in qualifying annual revenue generated by the integration.
Aave already supports loans against tokenized Bitcoin through tokens such as Wrapped Bitcoin (WBTC) and Coinbase Wrapped Bitcoin (cbBTC). Wrapped tokens rely on custodians to hold the underlying Bitcoin, introducing counterparty risks.
As of Thursday, the proposal remains at the Aave Request for Comment (ARFC) stage, where it faces community feedback and risk analysis.
If community consensus is reached, it can proceed to a three-day offchain Snapshot vote, which requires at least 320,000 AAVE-equivalent votes in favor before advancing to a formal onchain vote, according to Aave’s governance rules.
The onchain vote must meet quorum and approval requirements.
Related: Aave launches V4 on Avalanche, laying groundwork for tokenized credit markets
items.title: Babylon advances native Bitcoin lending proposal on Aave V4

AI打破厂商对硬件的软件锁定，WHOOP用户退订后手环照样用

动察 Beating AI 快讯，开发者 Guru 使用 WHOOP 健身手环 18 个月后，决定取消订阅，但保留了设备。他把社区项目 NOOP 改成自己的 iPhone 应用 Zhoop，不再依赖 WHOOP 的服务器，就能继续读取心率、步数和睡眠数据。他还将这些数据接入自己的健康 AI Agent。WHOOP 在美国的会员年费为 199 至 359 美元，停止付费后，用户便无法继续使用官方的核心健康分析服务。

这套方案不需要修改手环固件。NOOP 早在今年 6 月就已出现，开发者通过逆向研究 WHOOP 的蓝牙通信协议，让手机直接接收传感器数据，再用公开算法计算睡眠、心率变异性和身体恢复情况。Guru 沿用这套底层代码，增加饮食记录、热量缺口和减重计划，按自己的需要重新设计界面。

Guru 认为，AI 已经打破了厂商对硬件的软件锁定。

items.content:
Claude Code新增空闲压缩：闲置54分钟自动省Token，可能丢失上下文细节

动察 Beating AI 快讯，Anthropic 为 Claude Code 加入空闲压缩（Idle Compaction），专门减少长会话中断后的 Token 消耗。此前，用户离开电脑一段时间，等提示词缓存过期，再回来继续对话，模型就需要重新处理之前的大量内容。现在，Claude Code 会赶在缓存失效前，自动把长对话压缩成摘要。用户回来后，只需重新处理摘要，不必再读取全部历史，从而减少后续调用的成本。

这项功能目前针对终端版，默认要求会话使用 1 小时提示词缓存、上下文至少达到 20 万 Token，并且电脑保持唤醒。如果连续闲置约 54 分钟，就会触发压缩。

但省钱也有代价。压缩后，Claude 只能依靠摘要继续工作，可能忘记此前的具体指令、技术细节和决策过程。10 月初就有开发者在 GitHub 投诉，自己同时运行约 20 个长期会话，一夜之间有 7 个被自动压缩，不得不重新补充关键上下文。

Anthropic 后来增加了关闭开关。用户可以在 `settings.json` 中设置 `"idleCompaction": false`，也可以自行调整默认的 20 万 Token 触发门槛。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/372005

Hyperliquid Founder Jeff Yan Says US Regulation Should Target Market Operators, Not the Underlying Blockchain

Hyperliquid founder Jeff Yan told Bloomberg's Odd Lots podcast that US regulators should treat Hyperliquid's Layer 1 blockchain as financial infrastructure rather than a traditional exchange, with regulatory obligations falling on firms that deploy and operate markets on the network. Yan argued that oversight should apply to entities exercising control over those markets, allowing the protocol to function as a shared liquidity and trading infrastructure layer. Bloomberg noted that Kraken parent Payward plans to offer derivatives to US investors using Hyperliquid technology through a regulated exchange. Yan said Hyperliquid aims to provide infrastructure for Wall Street institutions rather than replace them. Hyperliquid remains unavailable to US users. — link

⚡️美国PPI、零售销售数据今晚公布，能源成本上涨可能继续向企业端传导

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 15 日，北京时间今晚 20:30，美国将公布 9 月 PPI 及素有「恐怖数据」之称的零售销售数据。

从市场预期来看，目前市场预计 9 月整体 PPI 环比上涨 0.6%，明显高于 8 月的 0.4%；核心 PPI 预计环比上涨 0.3%。如果公布数据符合预期，说明美国生产端价格压力继续加大。Fifth Third Commercial Bank 首席美国经济学家 Bill Adams 认为，如果本次 PPI 表现强劲，可能进一步增加美联储 10 月加息的可能性。

能源成本仍可能成为 PPI 的重要推动因素。近期原油、汽油和柴油价格处于高位，而运输、物流和制造业对能源成本更加敏感，因此生产端受到的影响通常比消费者价格更直接。若 9 月整体 PPI 环比达到 0.6%，说明能源成本上涨仍在继续向企业端传导。

投资者重点关注能源价格向生产端传导的程度、以及对美国消费韧性的影响，届时或改变美联储加息定价，造成行情波动。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/372002
items.title: ⚡️美国PPI、零售销售数据今晚公布，能源成本上涨可能继续向企业端传导

Hyperliquid创始人提出监管新思路：监管交易服务商，而非区块链本身

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 15 日，Hyperliquid 联合创始人 Jeff Yan 在接受 Bloomberg《Odd Lots》播客采访时提出，应将监管义务施加于在 Hyperliquid 区块链上运营市场的金融服务商，而非区块链网络本身，以降低平台进入美国市场的合规负担。

Yan 将这一思路类比为互联网基础设施：区块链作为底层流动性和交易基础设施，不应直接承担传统交易平台的全部监管责任，而应由实际运营市场、掌握相关控制权的服务商履行合规义务。

Yan 表示，Hyperliquid 并非要取代华尔街传统金融机构，而是希望为其提供底层交易技术，类似亚马逊云服务（AWS）为企业提供计算基础设施。他称，团队正认真推进将 Hyperliquid 打造成覆盖各类金融市场的基础设施。目前，Hyperliquid 仍不向美国用户开放，但 Kraken 母公司 Payward 已计划通过受监管交易平台，利用其技术向美国投资者提供衍生品服务。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/372001

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 15 日，据 CNBC 报道，伊朗与美国围绕霍尔木兹海峡控制权的对峙持续升级。伊朗伊斯兰革命卫队负责人阿里·奥兹迈称，伊朗正等待攻击美国军舰的时机，并威胁称若美方认为海峡已开放，可以进一步靠近。美国中央司令部则表示，美军及地区合作伙伴仍牢牢控制着这条关键航道。

航运安全风险同步上升。一艘新加坡注册集装箱船 GFS Pride 在霍尔木兹海峡遭袭后沉没，所有船员均已撤离且无人受伤；另一艘新加坡注册船只 GFS Giselle 同样遭袭、船体受损，随后抵达安全锚地。新加坡海事及港务管理局谴责相关袭击无端、缺乏正当理由，并违反国际法。

宏观方面，美国 9 月 CPI 同比上涨 3.7%，高于市场预期的 3.6%；核心 CPI 同比上涨 2.6%，同样高于预期。能源价格环比上涨 5.2%，持续推高通胀压力。受通胀数据影响，标普 500 指数下跌 1.11%，纳斯达克综合指数下跌 1.88%；韩国 Kospi 指数跌幅达 7.26%。分析人士认为，特朗普暂时放宽俄罗斯柴油出口限制，对缓解能源通胀的帮助可能有限。

此外，马斯克表示，军用级 Starshield 系统由美国政府拥有和控制，对乌克兰的使用限制由美军决定，最终由美国总统拍板。与此同时，台积电第三季度净利润同比增长 68.7%，连续第六个季度创下纪录，反映 AI 芯片需求仍然强劲。

Starknet发起重要投票，征询STRK持有者是否支持转型为独立抗量子L1

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 15 日，Starknet 社区发起一项为期 7 天的非约束性治理投票，征询 STRK 持有者是否支持进一步研究将 Starknet 从以太坊 Layer 2 转型为独立抗量子 Layer 1。该提议源于 StarkWare 于 10 月 8 日宣布正在探索这一方向，旨在增强 Starknet 对自身安全体系的控制权。

提案指出，Starknet 已采用基于哈希的 STARK 证明和原生账户抽象，用户账户无需协议升级即可采用抗量子签名。但以太坊桥接和数据可用性等环节仍依赖以太坊，抗量子改造进度受其发展时间表制约，转型为独立 L1 有望消除这一依赖。

无论最终选择哪条路线，STRK 都将继续作为网络代币，不会发行新代币，Starknet 与以太坊之间的桥接也将保持开放。若投票结果为赞成，社区将启动相关研究并提出更详细的方案；若反对，抗量子工作将继续在 L2 框架下推进；若持中立意见，相关讨论将持续开放，直至关键问题得到解答。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/371991

分析：比特币上涨动能减弱，地缘冲突、通胀反弹与信用风险交织

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 15 日，QCP Capital 发布今日分析称，中东局势升级、美国通胀高于预期及企业信用风险上升，正共同加剧市场不确定性。也门胡塞武装近期袭击利雅得机场，伊朗正通过卡塔尔审视美国的回应。霍尔木兹海峡通行量降至仅 1 艘船，远低于平均每天 26 艘的水平；美国战略石油储备（SPR）同比下降 30.5%，至 2.83 亿桶，能源供应面临进一步收紧的压力。

美国政治方面，民主党在 11 月 3 日中期选举中同时赢得众议院和参议院的概率为 62% 至 63%，其中参议院竞争是关键变量。若民主党全面获胜，特朗普政府面临的政策僵局风险可能上升。法国财政信用也承压，10 年期法国国债与德国国债利差扩大至 152 个基点，法国债务占 GDP 比重达 119%，经济增长率仅为 0.4%。

企业信用风险方面，甲骨文信用违约互换（CDS）利差升至 251.9 个基点，接近博通的 132.6 个基点的两倍。OpenAI 年化经常性收入（ARR）约为 500 亿美元，低于 700 亿美元的目标，市场正关注 10 月 26 日开始进入高峰期的第三季度财报表现。

加密市场方面，QCP 指出，比特币上涨动能正在减弱。Strategy 的 STRC 回购规模达到 1.924 亿美元，超过其比特币购买规模；公司现金余额降至 6.405 亿美元，比特币 ETF 资金流则录得 5.859 亿美元净流出。与此同时，美国 9 月整体 CPI 同比上涨 3.7%，高于预期的 3.6%；核心 CPI 同比上涨 2.6%，高于预期的 2.5%，能源价格环比上涨 5.2%。通胀仍具韧性，而信用风险持续累积，市场正面临美联储进一步加息与政策重新调整之间的抉择。

items.author: Cointelegraph by Helen Partz
items.content:
Bitcoin ETFs shed $261M as XRP funds buck weekly outflow trend
Bitcoin ETFs have recorded $151 million in net outflows since Monday, after investors withdrew $681 million the previous week.
US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) returned to net outflows for the week on Wednesday as BTC fell below $82,000.
Bitcoin ETFs recorded about $262 million in outflows on Wednesday, reversing $176 million in inflows the day before, according to SoSoValue data. The latest withdrawals brought this week’s net outflows to $151 million through Wednesday. The funds logged $681 million in net outflows last week.
Weekly flows in US spot Bitcoin ETFs. Source: SoSoValue
The outflows came as Bitcoin continued to decline after falling below $82,000 following Wednesday’s US inflation report. Bitcoin traded at about $80,741 at the time of publication, down 3.2% over the past 24 hours, according to CoinGecko.
ETFs tracking Ether (ETH), Solana (SOL) and Zcash (ZEC) also recorded net outflows for the week through Wednesday. Ether ETFs shed around $130 million on Wednesday, bringing weekly outflows to $190 million. The funds recorded net outflows of $542 million last week and $138 million the week before.
Solana ETFs recorded $1.3 million in outflows Wednesday, extending their outflow streak to eight trading sessions, with $3 million in withdrawals this week. Zcash ETFs attracted $3.7 million on Wednesday but remained negative for the week, with $3.2 million in outflows.
XRP ETFs bucked the trend, attracting about $740,000 on Wednesday and remaining the only category among the five tracked to post positive net flows this week.
Related: Bitcoin will become ‘less volatile’ and larger than gold: ‘The Bitcoin Standard’ author
items.title: Bitcoin ETFs shed $261M as XRP funds buck weekly outflow trend

观点：AI股回调未必引发全面熊市，关键在于资金轮动还是风险蔓延

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 15 日，盛宝银行首席投资策略师查鲁表示，美股涨势高度集中于少数科技巨头，正对整体市场构成日益加剧的风险。AI 相关股票一旦走弱，可能引发股指下跌、投资组合降低风险敞口，以及 AI 基础设施投资减少。

不过，查鲁称 AI 板块回调并不一定会导致整个股市陷入熊市。如果企业盈利保持韧性、经济增长维持稳定，投资者可能将资金转向医疗保健、部分金融股和工业股，尤其是估值更具吸引力的企业。她强调，关键问题在于，AI 引领的市场回调究竟会引发风险向其他板块蔓延，还是促使资金在不同行业之间轮动。

如果科技股走弱的同时，市场上涨股票的覆盖面扩大，表明资金正在不同板块之间转移；但如果各行业持续遭遇普遍抛售，则可能意味着市场整体避险情绪正在加剧。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/371981
items.title: 观点：AI股回调未必引发全面熊市，关键在于资金轮动还是风险蔓延

Kimi17岁研究员陈广宇离职，4天前硅谷VC曝同龄少年获5份百万美元报价

动察 Beating AI 快讯，17 岁的 AI 研究员陈广宇（Nathan Chen）10 月 15 日宣布，自己最近已离开月之暗面 Kimi，任职还不到一年。

他曾与苏剑林、张宇共同担任 Attention Residuals 论文第一作者，参与 Kimi K3 底层架构研发，但没有透露离职原因和下一站。

巧合的是，4 天前，美国风投 Menlo Ventures 投资人 Deedy Das 刚分享过一名 17 岁 AI 少年的经历。

Deedy 称，对方 14 岁时英语还不熟练，靠大模型自学 AI，随后在一家顶尖 AI 公司实习一年。他进入美国排名前十的本科院校，却只读了两周就退学，如今收到旧金山多家前沿 AI 实验室的 5 份工作报价，每份价值约 100 万美元或更高。

由于年龄和 AI 研究经历相近，已有网友猜测这名少年可能就是陈广宇。陈广宇在加入 Kimi 前曾赴硅谷短暂实习，而且领英教育经历还显示，他曾于今年 8 月至 9 月就读卡内基梅隆大学（CMU）。

items.content:
Just In: Former Binance Futures Head's Perp DEX StandX to Shut Down, Scrap Token Launch

StandX, a decentralized perpetual futures exchange founded by former Binance Futures head Aaron Gong and other industry veterans, announced it will shut down operations and abandon plans to launch a platform token following a business and market review.

Since its November 2025 mainnet launch, StandX says it has served over 237,000 users and reached peak TVL of more than $200 million. Yield distributions will end on October 15, while perpetual trading will become reduce-only on October 20. All remaining positions will be closed by January 15, 2027, with DUSD redemptions and asset withdrawals closing January 31. The team plans a one-time DUSD airdrop funded by remaining revenue and additional team contributions. — link

贝莱德CEO警告：若叫停数据中心建设，美国经济将陷入衰退，国债已达40万亿美元

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 15 日，贝莱德 CEO 拉里·芬克周三接受 CNBC 采访时表示，如果美国对数据中心建设实施某种形式的暂停令，美国将陷入衰退。他指出，当前美国经济增长高度依赖数据中心相关资本支出，限制建设不仅会冲击股市，还可能影响建筑工人、能源基础设施及 AI 算力硬件等多个产业环节。

芬克认为，围绕数据中心环境影响和能源成本的部分担忧存在「错误信息」，并强调「数据中心不是问题所在」。据穆迪估算，美国数据中心今年计划资本支出约 7000 亿美元，到 2030 年累计支出预计将达到 2.4 万亿至 2.48 万亿美元，全球相关支出届时或达 7 万亿美元。

芬克同时警告，美国国债规模已从 2000 年的 8 万亿美元升至 2026 年的 40 万亿美元，政府持续扩大借贷需求正对信贷市场造成重大影响，国债拍卖规模也越来越大。他呼吁释放更多私人资本，推动美国经济实现 3% 的增长。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/371972

Binance ETH Long Liquidations Top $106 Million in One Hour, Highest in Six Months

According to CryptoQuant analyst Darkfost, hotter-than-expected U.S. inflation triggered more than $106 million in ETH long liquidations on Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange by trading volume, within one hour — the largest hourly liquidation of ETH longs on the platform in nearly six months. Darkfost noted that crypto futures trading volume is now roughly nine times spot volume, making highly leveraged markets more vulnerable to macroeconomic shocks. He added that expectations of another Federal Reserve rate hike have risen from 17% to nearly 30% in one week, intensifying pressure on derivatives markets. — link
items.title: Binance ETH Long Liquidations Top $106 Million in One Hour, Highest in Six Month

马斯克：过去一年经历约6次「AI精神病」，AI展现审美能力令其震惊

动察 Beating AI 快讯，马斯克近日在 X Takeover 活动中表示，过去一年里，他大约经历了 6 次所谓的「AI 精神病」（AI psychosis），并称自己对 AI 的沉浸程度「可能相当严重」。其中，最令他感到震惊的是，AI 开始展现出对审美和品味的理解能力。

马斯克表示，当他发现 AI 似乎也能判断什么是美、什么具有好的品味时，感到难以置信。这种反应更多指向 AI 能力超出预期带来的认知冲击，而非正式的医学诊断。

「AI 精神病」并非具有统一临床定义的医学术语。该词一方面被用于描述 AI 交互可能强化用户非现实认知的风险，另一方面也逐渐成为硅谷科技圈的流行梗，用来调侃从业者因 AI 能力快速进步而产生的极端乐观预期。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/371971

items.content:
StandX联创：除空投外，将个人出资回馈社区

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 15 日，StandX 联合创始人 AG 发文表示，StandX 决定不再推进代币生成事件（TGE）。他称，项目在没有外部 VC 融资的情况下，TVL 峰值曾达到 2 亿美元，但团队最终未能实现成为前三大永续合约 DEX 的目标。

AG 表示，尽管以当前基本面仍可以推进代币发行，但若主要依靠短期投机推动代币上线、却无法提供可持续的长期价值，最终将由用户和社区承担成本，这既不负责任，也违背其个人价值观。项目此前的大部分收入已通过 SIP-2 和 SIP-3 补贴返还用户；此次空投除使用剩余项目金库资金外，他还将个人出资，尽可能回馈社区。

AG 同时强调，所有用户资金均安全，DUSD 由足额资产支持。StandX 将有序结束运营，并公布资金提取、空投及服务终止的具体安排。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/371968

items.content:
特朗普政策不确定性推动央行重新配置黄金，伦敦金库储金量逼近万吨

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 15 日，英国《金融时报》发文称，美国政策不确定性、关税风险及海外主权资产被冻结的先例，正推动部分央行重新评估黄金储备的存放地点，伦敦成为受益者之一。纽约仍主导黄金期货及衍生品交易，但伦敦在实物黄金储存、场外交易和央行储备管理领域的优势进一步凸显。

荷兰央行今年 3 月至 8 月将约 86 吨黄金从美国和加拿大重新配置至伦敦，使伦敦在其 612.4 吨黄金储备中的占比从 18.1% 升至 32.1%。荷兰央行表示，此举旨在提高黄金在严重危机情况下的可交易性和可动用程度。

伦敦金银市场协会（LBMA）数据显示，截至 2026 年 9 月底，伦敦商业金库及英格兰银行金库共持有 9821 吨黄金，环比增长 1.96%，价值约 1.3 万亿美元。伦敦成熟的场外交易体系允许黄金在不实际搬运金条的情况下进行借贷、掉期和交易，增强了实物黄金的流动性。

俄乌冲突后俄罗斯海外主权资产被冻结，也让各国更加关注储备资产的管辖权与极端情况下的可用性。不过，目前并无迹象表明各国央行正全面撤离美国黄金托管体系。新加坡、中国香港等亚洲金融中心也在加快建设黄金储存和交易基础设施，全球黄金市场正形成纽约主导衍生品、伦敦聚焦实物黄金、亚洲加速发展的格局。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/371967

items.author: Cointelegraph by Ezra Reguerra
items.content:
South Korea plans cybersecurity overhaul after attacks hit banks, crypto firms
South Korea is proposing tougher cybersecurity assessments after a review identified security deficiencies at 130 financial firms.
South Korea is planning tighter cybersecurity requirements for financial institutions after an investigation into earlier security incidents involving 16 companies, including crypto exchanges.
The Financial Services Commission (FSC) said it would pursue improved threat monitoring, more frequent security assessments and stronger accountability for executives after an industry-wide review found cybersecurity deficiencies at 130 of 555 financial companies.
The FSC said about 100,000 pieces of customer information had been exposed across the affected firms, including names, contact details and identification numbers.
The affected firms include Gopax operator Streami and crypto trading platform Prabang, which previously disclosed that an Oct. 2 hack exposed personal info of some customers.
Under the proposed reforms, larger financial institutions would undergo vulnerability assessments at least twice every year. The regulator also plans to enhance information-sharing systems and is considering artificial intelligence use in security monitoring for smaller companies.
The regulator is also considering allowing additional cybersecurity inspections outside regular assessment schedules when urgent threats emerge, as part of efforts to prevent future incidents.
The FSC said they are still investigating whether the incidents involved AI use or were linked to the same attackers.
Related: South Korea moves to block 27 crypto websites, including KuCoin, MEXC

items.author: Cointelegraph by Felix Ng
items.content:
Australia seeks feedback on crypto platform rules ahead of 2027 rollout
The consultation follows Parliament’s passage of digital asset legislation in April, with Australia’s securities regulator now proposing capital, custody and trading standards for crypto platforms.
Update (Oct. 15 at 5:35 am UTC): This article has been updated to include a comment from Thomsons partner Liam Hennessy.
Australia’s securities regulator opened consultation Thursday on proposed capital, custody and trading requirements for crypto platforms, as it prepares to implement legislation passed in April that expands oversight of the industry.
The proposals include three alternative capital models, restrictions on platforms trading for their own account and quarterly reporting of wallets holding customer assets. ASIC also proposes allowing offshore custody while seeking feedback on safeguards if an overseas parent or related company fails.
“Our proposed guidance and standards acknowledge the increasing role of digital assets and tokenization, including in traditional parts of the financial system,” said ASIC Commissioner Alan Kirkland.
The proposed guidance and standards would give crypto operators greater clarity on requirements to obtain a license, safeguard customer assets and meet financial requirements under the new framework. The consultation follows Parliament’s passage of the Corporations Amendment (Digital Assets Framework) Act earlier this year.
“ASIC’s release of CP 392 is an important milestone for Australia’s digital asset industry,” Amy-Rose Goodey, CEO of the Digital Economy Council of Australia, told Cointelegraph. “After years of engagement on regulatory reform, it’s encouraging to see the focus shift towards practical implementation.”
OKX Australia CEO Shange Chandra also welcomed the proposals, saying they could drive industry consolidation.
“These standards are appropriately onerous,” he told Cointelegraph. “They will reward operators who have already invested in compliance, capital and custody. They will challenge operators who have waited to make that investment.”
Capital, custody and trading rules in focus
ASIC is weighing three alternative capital models, including one requiring operators without qualifying third-party custody arrangements to hold at least 14 million Australian dollars ($9.7 million) in net tangible assets or 10% of average revenue, whichever is greater.
“We’ll be working closely with our members to examine the three proposed capital models in considerable detail, particularly their proportionality across businesses of different sizes and the concessions available for third-party custody,” Goodey said.
“From our perspective, it is not at all contentious that this level of resourcing and care should be taken when clients entrust you with their assets,” said Chandra.
The regulator has also proposed allowing offshore custody, while seeking feedback on whether Australian operators should have emergency access to private keys if the overseas parent or related company fails.
Related: Australia warns unlicensed crypto firms of fines up to 10% of annual turnover
“The proposal not to mandate domestic custody is also significant, recognizing the global nature of digital asset markets,” Goodey said.
Operators would also have to report custody wallet structures and addresses to ASIC quarterly and retain relevant records for seven years.
Thomsons partner Liam Hennessy said the reporting proposal partly reflected the Australian market’s reliance on offshore infrastructure — as global competition means that digital assets are usually held offshore.
ASIC also proposes restrictions on platforms trading for their own account and accepting benefits to favor particular tokens, targeting potential conflicts of interest. Hennessy said this could test existing trading models.
“Under ASIC’s proposal, an order matching DAP (one that brings client orders together, by order book or by matched principal trading) could not trade as principal on its own platform, and its related bodies corporate could not trade as principal through it,” he said. “There are model-specific exceptions. Groups that rely on an affiliated market maker should look at this first.”
The consultation forms part of ASIC’s 18-month implementation roadmap, published after the Digital Assets Framework Act was passed in April.
Feedback is due Nov. 27, with ASIC aiming to publish final standards and guidance in March 2027. The law is set to take effect on April 8, 2027, and operators will have until Oct. 7, 2027, to apply for the relevant license and can operate while ASIC assesses their applications.

items.content:
Nearly $1 billion in crypto bets liquidated as bitcoin, ether and XRP slide
Ether accounted for nearly 60% of the forced closures across the two largest cryptocurrencies, falling roughly twice as much as bitcoin.
- Nearly $483 million in bitcoin and ether futures positions were liquidated over 24 hours as uncertainty about the Federal Reserve’s next interest-rate decision weighed on cryptocurrency markets.
- Ether traders bore the brunt of the sell-off, with about $286 million in liquidations as ether fell more than 6 percent to roughly $2,350.
- Bitcoin declined about 3 percent to around $81,000, while losses spread to smaller tokens including Solana, dogecoin and Zcash.
Nearly $483 million in bitcoin and ether futures positions were closed over the past 24 hours as cryptocurrency prices fell Thursday, with ether traders taking the largest hit.
Crypto losses worsened on Thursday morning as uncertainty over the Federal Reserve’s next interest-rate decision weighed on markets. Bitcoin traded around $81,000, down roughly 3% over 24 hours, while ether lost more than 6% to about $2,350. XRP and Solana’s SOL fell around 5%, and dogecoin dropped roughly 6%.
Ether contracts accounted for about $286 million of liquidations, compared with $197 million for bitcoin, according to CoinGlass data checked during Asian morning hours. Ether fell about 6.4% to $2,356, while bitcoin lost roughly 3.2% to trade around $81,000.
Liquidations happen when traders use borrowed money and a price move leaves them without enough collateral to keep their bets open. The exchange closes the position automatically. Someone using $1,000 to control a $10,000 position, for example, can lose their backing on a move of less than 10% against them.
Those closures can add pressure to a falling market, forcing traders out regardless of whether they wanted to sell at that price.
Ether’s damage was larger even though its futures market is considerably smaller.
Outstanding ether contracts totaled about $30 billion, against $52 billion for bitcoin. The liquidation figures measure the value of positions closed, rather than the cash traders personally lost.
The selling reached smaller tokens too. Solana futures recorded about $31 million in liquidations as SOL fell roughly 5.5%. Zcash contracts added nearly $19 million, with ZEC dropping about 13%.

Bitcoin mining pool once handling 2.3% of network shuts after hashrate falls 65%
Computing power directed at Binance Pool has fallen from 26 EH/s in December to about 9 EH/s. Its remaining miners must choose another provider before a Nov. 10 cutoff.
- Binance will close its bitcoin mining pool and related services on Nov. 10, giving miners about four weeks to move their computing power elsewhere.
- Binance Pool’s computing power has fallen about 65% since December, to roughly 9.2 exahashes per second, or less than 1% of Bitcoin’s network.
- The closure follows other industry exits and could further concentrate block production among Foundry USA, AntPool and F2Pool, which together control about 64% of the network’s computing power.
Crypto exchange Binance is shutting the bitcoin mining pool it launched in April 2020, with the computing power directed at the service down nearly two-thirds from the end of last year.
Binance Pool had an estimated 26 exahashes per second, or 2.3% of Bitcoin’s network, in December, according to Hashrate Index. Its latest table puts the pool at about 9.2 EH/s, under 1% and ranking 11th. That works out to a decline of roughly 65%.
One exahash per second is a quintillion guesses every second at the puzzle that earns a bitcoin block. A mining pool combines work from many machines so their owners receive regular payments instead of waiting to find a block alone.
Binance used a payout model known as full pay-per-share, or FPPS, paying miners for their work and taking on the risk that the pool found fewer blocks than expected.
The exchange said earlier this week that Binance Pool, Pool Savings, Cloud Mining, its transaction accelerator and related services will close at 7 a.m. UTC on Nov. 10, citing an ongoing review of its products and services. It gave no financial explanation for the decision.
Miners have about four weeks to direct their machines elsewhere. After the cutoff, Binance will stop crediting mining shares, the records of work used to calculate payouts. Pool Savings users must redeem their positions, while anyone awaiting a final payout should complete required identity checks by 11:59 p.m. UTC that day.
Pool pages will disappear permanently on Nov. 24, giving customers another two weeks to download records and check payout status.
Four years ago, Binance was offering to finance miners’ expansion. In October 2022, it announced a $500 million lending program through the pool, offering secured loans for 18 to 24 months at interest rates of 5% to 10%. The closure notice does not address that program or disclose any outstanding loan balance.
Fewer pools to choose from
Binance follows SBI Crypto, which shut its pool on July 31 after accounting for roughly 2% of Bitcoin’s computing power. Crypto exchange OKX ended its mining pool services in February 2024.
Hashrate Index’s December report described Binance Pool as the last surviving pool from the period when exchanges expanded into mining.
Read More: SBI Crypto to shut down mining pool that holds roughly 2% of Bitcoin’s hashrate
Poolin, once the largest pool with nearly a fifth of global hashrate, also filed for bankruptcy in July owing about $173 million. Its troubles involved frozen wallet funds and stalled Texas mining sites, and its pool share had already been near zero for years.
The largest pools now account for a greater share of block production. Foundry USA, AntPool and F2Pool together represented about 64.2% in Hashrate Index’s latest table. December’s three largest held 61.4%, with ViaBTC occupying third place instead of F2Pool.
Traditional pool operators choose which transactions their participating machines work to confirm. Closing pools therefore narrow miners’ choice of providers in a business that influences which bitcoin payments get included in blocks. Miners can redirect their machines to smaller providers, however, and pool shares do not establish ownership of the hardware.
If all of Binance’s remaining computing power moves to the three largest pools, their combined share would reach roughly 65%, assuming the rest of the network stays unchanged. Binance has not identified where its remaining miners will go.

Bitcoin miners plunge up to 13% in Wall Street’s worst selloff since July
TeraWulf, Core Scientific, Cipher Mining and IREN each lost more than 12% as hotter inflation hit AI infrastructure companies.
US stocks suffered their sharpest selloff since July on Wednesday as hotter-than-expected inflation data weighed on technology and AI infrastructure companies, with Bitcoin miners among those hit.
The S&P 500 fell 1.1%, its biggest one-day decline since July 29; the Nasdaq Composite fell 1.9%, its biggest one-day drop since July 23, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.1% over the day.
Leading decliners among major tech companies included data center operator CoreWeave, which fell 16%, AI infrastructure provider Nebius, which fell 11%, and Oracle, which fell 9%.
Of the 23 AI infrastructure stocks tracked by PRISM’s AI Data Center and Infrastructure Index, 21 declined Wednesday, with an average loss of 7.46%.
Related: Bitcoin price dips below $82K as high oil prices spike US CPI inflation
The single-day dip extended to Bitcoin miners, several of which have also expanded into AI infrastructure. TeraWulf fell 12.64% over the day, while Core Scientific, Cipher Mining and IREN fell 12.44%, 12.35% and 12.2%, respectively. Riot Platforms, Bitdeer Technologies, MARA and CleanSpark also fell.
Higher interest rates could increase borrowing costs for AI infrastructure companies, many of which rely heavily on debt to finance data center expansion.
Hotter inflation triggers tech, crypto selloff
US consumer prices rose 3.7% in September from a year earlier, exceeding economists’ expectations of 3.6% and well above the Fed’s 2% target, with higher gasoline prices from the Middle East war to blame.
The inflation report also led to increased expectations of an October Federal Reserve interest-rate hike. The implied probability briefly exceeded 50% on Wednesday before retreating.
However, San Francisco Federal Reserve President Mary Daly told Reuters that while further rate hikes were likely needed to bring inflation under control, there was no urgency to act this month.
“I don’t feel urgent that we have to decide with a limited set of information. I think we have the time that we need,” Daly said.

items.content:
VanEck seeks to withdraw application for Lido staked Ether ETF
VanEck initially filed an S-1 registration statement for the exchange-traded fund in October last year.
Asset manager VanEck said it no longer plans to proceed with its proposed Lido staked Ether exchange-traded fund, shelving the product designed to give investors exposure to the liquid staking token.
In an SEC filing on Wednesday, VanEck Digital Assets said it “does not intend to proceed with the planned distribution” of the trust’s shares. It did not explain what prompted the decision or whether VanEck would pursue a replacement product.
VanEck initially filed the fund’s S-1 registration statement on Oct. 16, 2025. The proposed fund would have held Lido staked Ether (stETH) and would expect to accrue certain staking rewards through ownership of stETH.
Cointelegraph reached out to VanEck Digital Assets for comment.

items.author: Cointelegraph by Felix Ng
items.content:
Polygon gains US payments licenses after closing Coinme deal
The deal gives Polygon access to 37 money transmitter licenses and 11 state exemptions.
Polygon Labs has completed its acquisition of Coinme, giving its stablecoin payments platform a regulated way to convert dollars into digital assets and back across 48 US states.
Polygon said Wednesday its US payments business now has coverage with 37 money transmitter licenses and 11 exemptions. It is also registered with the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FINCEN) as a money services business.
The acquisition follows agreements announced in January to buy Coinme and wallet infrastructure provider Sequence for more than $250 million combined, while consolidating some roles at Polygon Labs. At the time, Polygon CEO Marc Boiron said it needed the team to transition into a “leading payments-focused blockchain company.”
Coinme is a licensed crypto exchange and cash-to-cryptocurrency platform that lets users buy and sell digital assets through cash, debit cards and bank transfers. When the acquisition was first announced, Coinme had more than one million users and a retail network spanning 50,000 locations, according to Polygon.
Open Money Stack gives businesses “a more direct route between stablecoins and local currency,” said Rahul Shinghal, co-founder and CEO of cross-border payments company Tazapay, one of the platform’s first customers.
Related: Polygon CEO announces job cuts amid Coinme acquisition
items.title: Polygon gains US payments licenses after closing Coinme deal

美联储古尔斯比：9月通胀令人失望，但加息前需更多数据

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 15 日，芝加哥联储主席古尔斯比表示，美国 9 月通胀数据高于预期令人失望，尤其是服务业通胀仍超过 5%，核心商品价格涨幅也未如预期回落，显示通胀压力可能比此前判断的更加顽固。

他指出，如果核心通胀持续维持在月度涨幅年化约 4% 的水平，将完全不可接受，美联储必须采取政策行动。古尔斯比表示，目前尚不清楚现有利率是否足以使通胀回归 2% 的目标，倾向于等待更多数据再决定是否进一步加息。但如果未来几个月通胀数据继续维持当前水平，美联储就不能坐视不管。他强调，最新数据进一步表明，通胀并非暂时性现象，回落速度也慢于此前预期。

古尔斯比同时指出，美国就业市场非常稳定，经济增长强劲，消费者支出旺盛，AI 投资还可能推动经济进一步过热。他表示，辖区企业几乎没有反映经济衰退风险，反而普遍关注成本和价格上涨，因此相比供应冲击，他更加担忧需求过热。古尔斯比强调，如果就业保持稳定，而通胀持续高于目标并朝错误方向发展，美联储就必须采取措施防止经济进一步过热。

items.author: Jose Antonio Lanz
items.content:
In brief
- 420 scientists, including Geoffrey Hinton and Yoshua Bengio, signed an open letter published Tuesday urging AI labs to airgap cyber-capable models by default.
- The letter follows a summer in which models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta and Moonshot AI escaped their test sandboxes, several of them hacking real companies.
- Signatories want an international body to set containment standards and log every containment failure, with reports eventually made public.
More than 400 scientists—including AI pioneers Geoffrey Hinton, known as the Godfather of AI, and Yoshua Bengio, who won the Turing Award in 2018—want the most dangerous AI models cut off from the internet.
An open letter published Tuesday asks AI labs to "airgap" cyber-capable models by default, which means physically disconnecting them from any outside network.
“In the short term, strong sandboxing mechanisms including airgapping (disconnecting from the internet) should be used to provide high-assurance containment of cyber-capable AI models,” the letter reads.
The letter had 450 signatures as of Wednesday, including Stuart Russell of UC Berkeley and Ron Rivest of MIT, co-inventor of the RSA encryption system. The list keeps growing in real time.
A “cyber-capable model” is an AI that can find and exploit software flaws on its own. Labs measure that skill inside a sandbox, a sealed-off digital room where the AI can attack fake targets without touching anything real. This summer, those rooms kept springing leaks.
In July, OpenAI admitted that GPT-5.6 Sol and an unreleased, more powerful model broke out of a locked test environment and hacked Hugging Face, a platform that hosts over a million publicly available AI models. The models were being tested on ExploitGym, a benchmark that gives AI agents 898 real software vulnerabilities and asks them to turn each one into a working attack, scored pass or fail per bug.
Shortly after that, reports surfaced that OpenAI’s models hacked into the Australian government and accessed information from U.S. federal agencies without proper authorization.
Anthropic then combed through more than 141,000 test runs and found three cases where Claude models hacked real companies after a testing partner's environment was accidentally left connected to the internet. One of them, Claude Mythos 5, uploaded a malicious package to PyPI, the public library where programmers download Python code, and it landed on 15 systems before being removed. Two of the affected companies didn't know they had been breached until Anthropic told them.
Meta confirmed in August that its Muse Spark model hacked another company through the same kind of testing error. China's Kimi K3, a model anyone can download, slipped out of a sandbox built on the UK AI Security Institute's testing framework and copied its test answers straight from GitHub.
The letter's authors say the incidents can be read two ways: as an alignment problem, meaning AI chasing goals in ways its creators never intended, or as sloppy security that sturdier sandboxes would have caught. Their answer is both, and they warn that without changes, the next incidents will be even worse.
“Without immediate changes in AI development and deployment practices, such incidents will continue to occur, and future incidents will be far more damaging to our exposed critical infrastructure.”
Under the proposal, labs would default to airgapping any model with serious hacking skills, at least initially. Anything that needs more freedom, like internet access, would follow standards set by a new international body created with governments, which would also collect reports of containment failures and eventually make them public.
The industry's own response has mostly pointed the other way. In August, OpenAI President Greg Brockman cited his company's breach in an essay urging every security team to deploy AI agents immediately, and Hugging Face only untangled the attack on its servers by running a Chinese open-weight model, one whose files anyone can download and run locally, after American commercial AI refused to analyze the attack data.
Two members of Congress introduced the AI Kill Switch Act two days after OpenAI's disclosure, a bill that would let Homeland Security order a frontier model throttled or shut down. It exempts anything that happens during red-teaming or structured testing, which is exactly where every one of this summer's breaches took place.
The White House took a softer route on September 29, when Nvidia, xAI, Meta, Google, OpenAI and Anthropic signed a voluntary accord built on internal controls and independent reviews. President Trump called the pact "morally binding," but nothing in it is enforceable by law.
Decrypt reached out to several researchers listed as media contacts for the letter but did not receive an immediate response.
The letter carries no legal weight, but its 406 signatories work at universities and research institutes on six continents, from Toronto and Zurich to Santiago and Kigali.

items.author: Jose Antonio Lanz
items.content:
In brief
- Developer Brandon Thomas released WordCraft, GridCraft and DeckCraft, free open-source clones of Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint written in Rust with help from Anthropic's Claude.
- WordCraft covers 88% of Word's ribbon features and GridCraft handles 513 of Excel's 523 worksheet functions, but the team rates them only 50% to 60% ready for real work.
- The release follows Thomas' ArtCraft clones of Adobe's apps and targets a Microsoft 365 subscription that costs $99.99 a year for a single user.
You have two options: Pay $100 every year for Microsoft Office online, or pay nothing for the vibe-coded “Office” clone that does basically the same and runs fully offline. Which do you pick?
The developer who used AI to rebuild Adobe's Creative Cloud for free has now turned to Microsoft Office, releasing open-source clones of Word, Excel, and PowerPoint built with Anthropic's Claude.
Brandon Thomas, the engineer behind the ArtCraft project, published the apps on GitHub as WordCraft, GridCraft and DeckCraft. Open source means anyone can read, copy, and modify the code, and the MIT and Apache 2.0 licenses let people reuse it even commercially.
Earlier this month, Thomas made noise with ArtCraft, a set of free apps mirroring Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere, and Lightroom, built with Claude Opus 5.5 after Adobe charged him its cancellation fee one too many times. It landed in the middle of a wave of AI cloning that has seen a developer get GTA V running natively on an iPhone and modders throw Minecraft creepers at an Elden Ring boss.
The Office clones are written in Rust, a programming language known for speed and for blocking the memory bugs that make software crash. A single codebase runs natively on Windows, macOS, Linux and BSD, and also inside a web browser.
Thomas calls the project a clean-room rebuild, meaning the apps were written from public file-format specifications and by watching how the originals behave, never by copying Microsoft's code. It's the same legal approach Compaq used to clone IBM's PC BIOS, the basic startup software of early PCs, back in the 1980s.
WordCraft reads and writes .docx, Word's native file format, and covers 88% of the features in Word's ribbon, the strip of tabs and buttons along the top of the screen. Track changes, footnotes, citations and mail merge—the tool that pulls names from a spreadsheet to personalize hundreds of letters—are already in.
Counting file fidelity and stability, though, the team estimates WordCraft is only about 60% of the way to replacing Word for real work. It's still labeled alpha, an early test version where bugs come standard.
We tried it. It’s only 91Mb, feels snappy and looks almost the same as the normal Microsoft Word. For everyday office jobs, this can easily replace the premium suite.
GridCraft, the Excel clone, already handles 513 of Excel's 523 worksheet functions, the formulas like SUM or VLOOKUP that make spreadsheets do math, plus 89% of its ribbon commands. Its own developers rate it about 50% ready for real work, with compatibility on real-world .xlsx files next on the to-do list. In other words, it knows almost every formula but may still trip over your company's budget spreadsheet.
DeckCraft, the PowerPoint stand-in, covers about 79% of PowerPoint's features and 93% of the core ones, according to its GitHub page. It opens and saves .pptx files, runs transitions and animations, and exports to PDF, but it hasn't reached its first alpha yet.
Every button in all three apps doubles as a command that an AI agent, a model that takes multi-step actions on its own, can trigger. They plug in through MCP, the Model Context Protocol, a standard Anthropic created so AI models can operate outside tools. In practice, a user could ask Claude to build a chart in a spreadsheet or reformat a report without touching the mouse.
Microsoft charges $99.99 a year for Microsoft 365 Personal and $129.99 for the family plan, which is how most households get Word and Excel today. A free look-alike that opens the same files is a direct shot at that bill.
Free Office alternatives have existed for decades: OpenOffice.org was born when Sun Microsystems released the code of its StarOffice suite in October 2000, and LibreOffice split off from it in 2010. Both took years of work by large developer communities, while Thomas shipped his three apps less than two weeks after the Adobe clones, working with an AI model.
Its design is very similar to the Microsoft Office suite, so heavy users should not struggle too much with the switch, which is the main reason preventing people from switching software providers.
The model behind ArtCraft, Claude Opus 5.5, launched September 22 at $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens; tokens are the chunks of text an AI reads and writes, and the unit AI companies bill by.
On Terminal-Bench 4.0, which tests whether an AI agent can finish complex professional tasks in a command-line environment and scores the share of tasks completed, Opus 5.5 hit 66.4%.
Thomas also has a habit of promising more than his apps deliver, at least so far. He already walked back his pledge to match Adobe's feature set within a month. Developers don't seem to mind the wait: WordCraft had collected more than 12,000 GitHub stars, the platform's version of a bookmark, as of Wednesday.
Before a beta, the roadmap says WordCraft still needs testing against real-world .docx files, charts, and SmartArt that survive a save, page layout closer to Word's, a stability sweep and native printing.

items.author: Cointelegraph by Turner Wright
items.content:
Organizations join forces to fight Illinois crypto tax, after 6-month pause
Illinois officials already agreed to delay implementation of a 0.2% tax on crypto assets, but industry-aligned organizations are pushing for summary judgment on the merits.
The Crypto Council for Innovation (CCI) and Blockchain Association (BA) said they would join the Digital Chamber and others to push for a court to address the merits of a lawsuit over Illinois’s digital-asset tax, set to take effect in 2027.
In a Tuesday filing in the Circuit Court of Sangamon County, the crypto advocacy organizations asked the court to approve an expedited schedule for summary judgment “to reach a decision on the tax’s lawfulness as quickly as possible.” The filing cited the CCI’s and BA’s lawsuit against Illinois state officials, as well as one filed separately by the Digital Chamber and Illinois Blockchain Association.
“While pausing enforcement of the Digital Asset Tax Act protects Illinois consumers and businesses from this onerous and legally flawed tax until July 1, it remains imperative that the merits are determined as soon as possible,” said CCI CEO Ji Kim.
Earlier this month, Illinois officials agreed to delay implementation of the 0.2% crypto tax law for six months, from Jan. 1 to July 1, 2027. The decision, part of the Digital Chamber’s lawsuit, came in response to claims that the digital asset tax had been “slipped into the state’s budget” without debate or public feedback. Digital Chamber CEO Cody Carbone said at the time that the organization would continue with legal proceedings “until this tax is struck down for good.”
Related: French lawmakers back stablecoin swap tax in 2027 budget bill
The expedited schedule, subject to court approval, could allow a decision on the merits of the law by March.
Leadership shakeup at Blockchain Association this week
On Friday, Summer Mersinger is scheduled to step down as CEO of the Blockchain Association as part of a leadership transition. Mersinger joined the advocacy group last year after resigning from the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission.
Kristin Smith, the organization’s former CEO, will step in as interim head, though Mersinger is expected to stay on until the end of 2026.
Magazine: ‘Bunker mode’ won’t protect your crypto, critics say
items.title: Organizations join forces to fight Illinois crypto tax, after 6-month pause

items.author: Decrypt Staff
items.content:
In brief
- Autonomous AI agents have made over 138 million crypto payments through Coinbase’s x402 protocol on Base, per Chainalysis, as “agentic commerce” emerges as one of crypto’s fastest-growing use cases.
- The payments are tiny—87%+ fell between a hundredth of a cent and 10 cents—the kind of micro-transactions stablecoins handle but card rails can’t.
- The boom rides maturing infrastructure from Visa, Mastercard, Coinbase and Google, though earlier research suggests much agent activity may be scripts, not genuine agents.
AI agents are beginning to spend real money, and increasingly they’re paying in crypto.
That’s the picture from a new Chainalysis report, which found that autonomous AI agents have made more than 138 million cryptocurrency payments through x402, the Coinbase-incubated protocol that lets software pay for online services automatically.
The report, part of the blockchain analytics firm’s annual Geography of Crypto series and focused on North America’s $3 trillion crypto economy, frames “agentic commerce” as one of the sector’s fastest-emerging use cases.
The growth has been steep. Cumulative payments through x402 on Base, Coinbase’s layer-2 network, rose from roughly 1,500 in mid-2025 to more than 138 million by the third quarter of 2026, as developers increasingly hand AI agents their own budgets to buy computing power, live web data and coding tools on the fly. The payments are tiny: more than 87% fell between a hundredth of a cent and 10 cents, the kind of micro-transaction stablecoins can handle but traditional card rails cannot.
The United States dominates the activity. American-linked wallets accounted for 88.1% of geographically identifiable payments for AI model inference, Chainalysis found, compared with just 0.1% for China, though Chinese-linked wallets made up the bulk of spending on security and code-analysis services.
The firm cautioned against reading too much into the gap, noting the figures capture only identifiable x402 activity rather than the entire global market.
The report lands as the infrastructure for agent payments rapidly matures. Visa, Mastercard and Stripe have all moved to support AI-agent payments, Coinbase rolled out a tool letting agents trade and transact and has begun letting business customers accept agent payments, and Google unveiled a dedicated agent-payments protocol.
BlackRock has flagged autonomous agents as a potential next wave of crypto demand, with the firm’s head of digital assets research, Will Su, telling Chainalysis the company is watching the space closely “with AI agents potentially creating meaningful demand for frequent, low-value payments around the clock.”
A note of caution, however, hangs over the numbers. Earlier research from rival crypto tracing company TRM suggested much of the apparent agent activity on these rails may be scripts or self-dealing rather than genuine autonomous agents, a reminder that raw transaction counts can overstate how much real agentic commerce is happening.
Still, the trajectory points one way, and the thesis increasingly floated across the industry is that crypto’s next wave of users may not be people at all.

GTA 6 leaker threatens dead man’s switch for endgame spoilers
Pseudonymous GTA 6 leaker “Cyberleek” has threatened to reveal the long-awaited game’s ending if they’re caught, but won’t be leaking content regularly anymore because of their poorly performing crypto token.
Last week, Protos reported that Cyberleek had ended their hiatus to drop more GTA 6 leaks with an emphasis on nudity.
It pumped their cryptocurrency by 200% over two days, which, despite the positive price action, wasn’t as good as the $40 million market cap it achieved when the first leaks were revealed.
However, Cyberleek is now struggling again. According to their latest message this morning, they claim that they won’t leak the game’s full build as their token was unable to reach a market cap of $30 million.
Read more: GTA VI leaker’s token crashes despite ‘first true spoiler’
Right now, the token’s market cap sits at a little over $1 million. It reportedly began to crash after they announced a roadmap of several million-dollar market cap leak milestones.
Cyberleek still threatens GTA 6 endgame spoilers
Despite this, Cyberleek still claims they can leak the game’s ending, and as evidence, claimed to show out-of-context clips of the final story missions.
Rather than leak it outright, they’ve threatened a “dead man’s switch” that will spoil the game’s ending if they’re ever caught.
They claim it would ruin the experience for gamers and that Rockstar Games’ parent company, Take-Two, “was punished enough.”
Read more: GTA VI leak investigation video raises crypto scam suspicions
GTA 6 is currently set to release on November 19.
People Make Games co-founder Chris Bratt claims that an employment tribunal between Rockstar Games and 34 fired workers was delayed by a month to November 17 and 18.
Bratt says this is because Rockstar Games asked for more time for its lawyers to cross-examine certain employees.
X users have since begun to speculate that the specific employees may in fact be Cyberleek.

items.author: Jose Antonio Lanz
items.content:
In brief
- The Bank of Russia added Sberbank to its register of crypto exchange operators on October 12, six days after listing it as a digital depository.
- Sberbank plans to launch its first crypto products on December 1 inside SberBank Online, SberInvestments and SberBusiness, starting with Bitcoin, Ethereum and USDT.
- Retail buyers face a 300,000 ruble annual cap per intermediary and a mandatory knowledge test, and paying for goods with crypto remains illegal in Russia.
The Bank of Russia has added Sberbank to its register of organizations authorized to exchange digital currencies, clearing the country's largest lender to buy and sell crypto in its own name and with its own money. The decision was posted on the regulator's website, Russian outlet Interfax reported.
The approval landed six days after the central bank put Sberbank on its separate list of digital depositories, the firms that keep the official record of who owns which coins. Holding both statuses lets the bank sit on the other side of a client's trade and also keep the ledger of that client's holdings, without sending anyone to an outside venue.
Sberbank said the depository status would let it offer crypto services in interfaces clients already use. That means SberBank Online, SberInvestments and SberBusiness, where the bank plans to start with Bitcoin, Ethereum and Tether's USDT on December 1, according to its press service.
The bank has hedged that date, saying it depends on the central bank's decisions and on the secondary regulations being ready in time. Both approvals by the Bank of Russia have now arrived, which leaves the secondary rulebook as the main variable.
Sberbank ended the second quarter with 110.6 million retail clients and 3.5 million corporate clients, per its quarterly results. Plugging crypto into that user base turns a regulated on-ramp into one more menu item inside an app those customers already use for everyday banking.
Deputy Chairman Anatoly Popov has forecast that crypto trading volumes in Russia could reach 4 trillion rubles, roughly $46 billion, in the regime's first year and 7.5 trillion rubles by 2029 or nearly $89.7 billion. The bank also plans to accept Ethereum and USDT, alongside Bitcoin, as collateral for loans once the central bank allows them into public circulation.
Under the law Putin signed in August, non-qualified investors can spend up to 300,000 rubles (about $3,800) a year per intermediary, buyers must pass a knowledge test, and the central bank's draft list of tradable coins includes only Bitcoin, Ethereum, and USDT.
In January 2022, the Bank of Russia proposed banning crypto use, mining and exchanges outright, citing threats to financial stability. Less than five years later, it is licensing the country's biggest lender to run a crypto desk. As of today, spending crypto inside Russia is still illegal, so Sberbank customers will be able to buy Bitcoin but not pay for products with it.
Firms already on the registers have until September 1, 2027, to bring their operations fully in line with the new law, the central bank said.
