Ripple adds Stripe-owned wallets to XRP Ledger as AI payments pass 14 million
The integration will let software pay for online services using XRP and RLUSD, while questions remain about how much real economic activity the transactions represent.
- Ripple and Stripe-owned Privy are partnering to let developers embed XRP Ledger wallets in payments apps, allowing customers to transfer XRP, the RLUSD stablecoin and other assets without setting up separate crypto wallets.
- The integration could also enable AI agents to hold funds and automatically pay for online data and services, with a Ripple executive saying such payments account for about 25 percent of XRP Ledger activity.
- Embedded wallets will still require funding to become active because each new XRP Ledger account must receive the network’s minimum reserve of 1 XRP, even if it will be used only for stablecoin payments.
Ripple is bringing wallet technology from Stripe-owned Privy to the XRP Ledger, allowing financial applications and AI agents to create accounts, hold cryptocurrencies and make payments without requiring users to manage their own wallet software.
The move will allow developers to create wallets inside their products and authorize transfers involving XRP, Ripple’s dollar-pegged RLUSD stablecoin and other assets issued on the network, per a release shared with CoinDesk.
That could let a payments company offer dollar-linked transfers without requiring customers to manage the secret keys that authorize spending.
Privy handles the wallet infrastructure, reducing what the app builder needs to develop itself. Additionally, it supports exporting keys or a recovery phrase so wallets can be moved elsewhere.
Companies could also give AI agents — or automated bots that complete a user’s given tasks — a bunch of funded wallets to pay for online services. Privy said in its documents that wallets operated from a company’s servers can let software hold and spend funds, including through x402, a payment standard for buying access to data and other services.
An agent requesting paid data, for example, can receive a payment request, authorize payment and obtain the data once that payment is verified. Software can pay for each request without a person opening a checkout page every time.
CoinDesk asked the XRP Ledger Foundation about applications using the integration and for data showing how much payment activity on the network comes from AI agents.
The announcement comes as developers report a sharp rise in such transactions on the XRP Ledger.
RippleX Head of Engineering J. Ayo Akinyele said on X last week that the network had processed more than 13 million agent payments through x402, representing roughly 25% of ledger activity.
Figures from the XRPL AI Hub, operated by payment infrastructure developer t54, showed more than 14.3 million cumulative transactions across 169 registered merchants as of Wednesday.
But the total value transferred was considerably smaller than the transaction count might suggest.
The dashboard recorded approximately 6,991 XRP and 12,752 RLUSD in cumulative payments. Many of the transactions therefore involve very small amounts, consistent with software paying for individual requests rather than large financial transfers.
Ripple began offering developers tools for these payments in June, letting agents create wallets, check balances and pay for services using XRP or RLUSD. In September, it expanded the kit to support a payment standard developed by Stripe and payments blockchain Tempo, including a way to fund repeated requests with XRP instead of settling each one separately.
Read More: Ripple adds XRP payments to Stripe and Tempo’s AI standard in new developer kit
Tuesday’s release said the companies will deepen the integration over time, including policy controls and tools for covering users’ network fees.
Meanwhile, creating a wallet inside an app still leaves a funding step before it can transact.
Privy’s documentation says a new XRP Ledger account must first receive the network’s minimum reserve, currently 1 XRP, meaning someone must supply that XRP to activate the account even if the customer only wants to send dollar-pegged stablecoins.

Anthropic主仓库弃用Git：日合并突破3万次，7个人花5个月完成系统迁移

动察 Beating AI 快讯，Claude 写代码的速度越来越快，已经让现有的 Git 系统跟不上。今年 5 月，Anthropic 主代码仓库平均每天合并约 2500 次变更，到 9 月已超过 3 万次，增至原来的 12 倍以上。为此，7 名工程师借助 Claude，在 5 个月内开发出新的版本控制系统 Scion，完成主仓库迁移，并推出配套的代码审查工具 Antique。

Anthropic 主分支的历史记录已接近 100GB，CI 系统每天需要检出约 2500 万次代码。公司曾部署数百台 Git 镜像服务器，仍难以应对持续增长的负载。Scion 改为按需获取代码，将提交、合并和历史查询交给服务端处理，避免每个任务都维护庞大的本地仓库。Anthropic 称，新系统所需的 CPU 和内存资源只有原 Git 镜像架构的 1/200，代码检出从分钟级缩短至秒级，CI 的 CPU 资源需求也下降了 25%。

Claude 也参与了新系统的开发。团队曾让 Claude Mythos Preview 重写一套人工编写的代码迁移程序，结果内存占用降至原来的 1/20，运行速度提升至 4 倍。参与项目的工程师都认为，Claude 的编码能力已超过自己，但他们仍负责架构决策和审核，尤其要阻止 Agent 违反系统约束、过度设计。

Scion 目前没有开源，也无法像 Git 一样离线工作。Anthropic 认为，这套系统主要适合有大量 Agent 并行编程的超大型仓库，其他公司若想采用，还需要重建代码审查、搜索和 CI 等配套工具。

GitLab 同日回应，正在开发兼容 Git 的新一代版本管理架构，希望保留现有开发流程，同时承受大量 Agent 并行工作带来的压力。该项目早在今年 6 月就与 Anthropic 展开技术合作，目前已进入私有测试阶段。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/371725

Solana sets Oct. 21 for Alpenglow upgrade targeting 150-millisecond finality
The switch will replace Solana’s existing validator voting system, remove vote transactions from blocks and could sharply change headline transaction counts even if user activity stays flat.
- Solana has scheduled its Alpenglow upgrade for Oct. 21, targeting transaction finality in about 150 milliseconds, though actual performance will depend on network conditions.
- Alpenglow will replace TowerBFT and move validator votes off-chain, which could sharply reduce Solana’s reported transaction count without reflecting a decline in user activity.
- Validators must use Agave 4.3.0 for the migration, while Firedancer and Frankendancer operators will need to switch software temporarily.
Solana has scheduled Oct. 21 for Alpenglow, a major upgrade aimed at making transactions irreversible in roughly 150 milliseconds by changing how the computers running the network agree on payments.
The updated timetable published by the Solana Foundation sets a date for replacing TowerBFT, the voting system Solana has used since its launch in 2020. The 150-millisecond figure remains a target, with actual performance depending on network conditions.
This matters as a Solana payment can already appear successful almost immediately. But Alpenglow aims to offer a stronger guarantee that it cannot be undone almost as quickly.
A merchant waiting for that assurance before accepting a payment, or a bridge before releasing funds on another blockchain, could act sooner.
As of today, validators, the computers that check transactions and help secure Solana, submit their votes as transactions recorded on the blockchain. Alpenglow will let them exchange votes directly and combine enough approvals into a certificate that finalizes a block after one or two voting rounds.
That could produce an odd result on activation day, however. Solana’s transaction count may fall sharply because validator votes disappear from blocks, even if people keep trading and making payments at the previous pace.
Read More: Solana’s 150-millisecond settlement upgrade reaches second public test network
Validators must also prepare for the switch. Operators need software built on Agave 4.3.0. Firedancer and Frankendancer, alternative programs used to run validators, will not support the initial migration, so their operators will need to switch temporarily.
Removing vote transactions also changes what validators pay. Their current voting charges of roughly 1 SOL per epoch will disappear, replaced by a flat admission fee of 0.8 SOL. An epoch is a period during which Solana assigns validators their network responsibilities.
The migration is scheduled for epoch 1064, expected to begin around 15:00 UTC on Oct. 21. Solana will continue using its old voting system for the first 5,000 slots, the short windows assigned for block production, before switching to Alpenglow roughly 18 minutes later.

Bitcoin climbs toward $84,000 after Fed’s Williams sees no rate hikes in 2027
ZEC led a broad bounce among major tokens, and Korean chipmakers snapped a five-day losing streak ahead of Thursday’s U.S. inflation data.
- Bitcoin rose 1.5 percent to nearly $83,900 after New York Fed President John Williams said he saw no need for further rate increases in 2027, weakening the dollar and lifting Asian markets.
- Zcash led major cryptocurrencies with a gain of nearly 7 percent, while Solana and Dogecoin each rose 2.5 percent and Ether added 2 percent.
- Thursday’s U.S. inflation report could determine whether the Fed raises rates once more this year and whether Bitcoin can retest $85,000.
Bitcoin rose 1.5% to just under $83,900 as of Wednesday Asian morning hours. New York Fed President John Williams said he saw no need for further rate hikes in 2027, which weakened the dollar and lifted stocks across Asia.
ZEC led the majors, jumping nearly 7% to about $1,270. SOL and DOGE each gained 2.5%, and ether rose 2% to about $2,520. XRP, BNB and HYPE added between 1% and 2%, while TRX lagged with a gain of less than 1%, according to CoinDesk data.
Williams did say one more hike this year may be appropriate. His comments still helped the S&P 500 pare its losses on Tuesday, and S&P 500 futures rose 0.2% with the index hovering near last week’s record.
Chipmakers recovered in Asia. Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix both rallied, snapping the five-day losing streak that had wiped out leveraged bets on chip stocks at crypto exchanges earlier this week. MSCI’s Asia Pacific equities index rose 0.7%, rebounding from two days of losses that had pushed it to its lowest close since August. Chip-equipment maker ASML reports earnings on Wednesday, and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing reports on Thursday.
Oil kept climbing. Brent rose 0.7% to about $106 a barrel as a flare-up in Middle East attacks raised doubts over a recovery in energy shipments from the Persian Gulf. U.S. crude rose for a fifth straight day.
Thursday’s U.S. inflation report is the next test of Williams’ view. A reading cool enough to rule out that last hike would give bitcoin room to retest $85,000.

items.content:
REA「复刻任何软件」遭实测检验：51次公开尝试，成功多是局部功能

动察 Beating AI 快讯，独立技术作者 quanglee 梳理了 51 次 REA 公开使用记录，发现所谓「复刻成功」，往往只意味着还原了一个功能。10 月 12 日，他发布调查结果：其中 9 次来自 REA 项目贡献者，均完成各自目标；另外 42 次独立尝试中，20 次完成、16 次部分完成、6 次失败。

问题出在「完成」的标准上。20 次独立成功案例中，9 次针对小游戏或小程序，6 次只还原了较大型软件的某项功能，还有 5 次甚至没有公开目标名称。一个表现不错的案例是解谜游戏 Untangle：Agent 分析其 167 KB 的程序后，做出了可玩的网页版，54 条技术结论有 52 条完全正确。但开发者事后审计发现，其中 10 个函数和字段名称并非来自 REA 的分析结果，可能是模型记住了原版的公开源码。

更复杂的项目需要投入大量工作。REA 贡献者在《东方永夜抄》的逆向工程中，让 1107 个函数中的 1106 个与原版机器码匹配，但耗时约两周，而且接续了此前的人工研究成果。另有人尝试复刻语音输入软件 Wispr Flow，虽然分析出了录音、转写和粘贴文字的部分流程，最终却只做出一份 64 行的 Python 脚本。原版依赖的云端模型、上下文处理和实时反馈等功能，都没有完整复现。

REA 可以帮助 Agent 调用 Ghidra、IDA 等工具，分析现有程序并重做部分功能。但一款商业软件的能力不只存在于安装包里，服务器上的模型、数据和复杂业务逻辑，无法靠反编译客户端直接还原。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/371701

火币HTX首席分析师Cloud：比特币方向待CPI定夺，8.1万美元下沿或先受考验

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 14 日，比特币自 10 月初 8.6 万美元附近回落，近几日在 8.1 万至 8.4 万美元区间震荡，同期美元走强、美债收益率维持高位。对此，火币 HTX 首席分析师 Cloud 认为，震荡区间向下打破的可能性更大。9 月 ISM 服务业物价支付指数升至 74.0，为 2022 年 7 月以来最高，10 月密歇根大学 1 年期通胀预期回升至 4.7%，价格分项与通胀预期同步走高，意味着本周四 CPI 超预期的概率不低。一旦兑现，年末加息定价将进一步强化，8.1 万美元下沿会先被测试；只有 CPI 低于预期，8.4 万美元上沿的突破才具备持续性。

近期芯片股持续下跌，主要源于 AI 资本开支节奏与硬件盈利预期在板块内部的重新定价，属于行业阿尔法事件。相比之下，比特币回撤幅度明显更小，说明其当前定价锚更偏向宏观流动性，与 AI 叙事的关联在减弱，两者的驱动因素正在分化。不过这种分化是阶段性的，一旦美元与长端利率重新主导定价，联动会迅速加强，周四晚间 CPI 公布正是最近的检验窗口。

items.content:
Bitunix分析师：CPI牵动利率预期，美元流动性将决定加密市场承压程度

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 14 日，全球资本市场面临的压力不再只是利率高低，而是政府与企业同步增加融资需求，正在争夺有限的市场资金。桥水创办人达利欧警告，美国今年约有 10 兆美元到期债务需要展期，另有约 2.1 兆美元新增借款需求；若投资人要求更高殖利率才愿意承接供给，政府利息负担便可能随再融资成本上升，形成债务与利率互相推升的循环。

股票市场也可能面临供给变化。保罗都铎琼斯预警，OpenAI、Anthropic 等 AI 企业潜在上市，加上企业二次发行，可能逆转过去由股票回购与并购支撑的供需结构。当政府发债、企业借款与新股发行同步增加，投资人必须在更多资产间分配资金，单靠成长预期支撑高估值的难度也将提高。

这种资金竞争同样直接影响加密市场。BTC 与 ETH 虽不直接承担美国政府的债务成本，但其估值仍受到美元流动性、实质利率与风险偏好牵动。若美债殖利率长期维持高位，资金可从债券取得更具吸引力的收益，加上 AI 企业持续吸收融资，可能限制流入加密资产的新增资金；若市场因融资压力转向避险，杠杆部位平仓也可能放大 BTC 及其他加密资产的波动。

短期焦点则落在美国 9 月 CPI。市场预估整体通膨年增率升至 3.6%，核心通膨约 2.5%，核心月增率则放缓至 0.2%。若核心物价温和，利率预期降温可能改善加密市场的风险偏好；若数据超预期，美元与殖利率再度走强，就可能对加密资产形成压力。即使通膨降温，也不代表流动性立即转松，后续仍须观察长端利率与资金配置是否同步改善。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/371696

items.author: theblockbeats
items.content:
20万星REA遭恶意仿冒：假冒安装包被报毒，已下载172次

动察 Beating AI 快讯，爆红的 AI 逆向工具 REA 遭到恶意仿冒。10 月 13 日，有开发者在 REA 官方 GitHub 仓库发出警告，称有人建立假冒仓库，提供携带疑似木马的 Windows 安装包。REA 近期的 GitHub Star 已突破 20 万，而假冒安装包在被举报时，下载计数已达到 172 次。

仿冒者注册了名为 `rea-tools/rea` 的 GitHub 仓库，与 REA 官网 `rea.tools` 极为相似，还直接复制了官方 README。他们在原有说明中增加「Windows 独立版」下载入口，提供一个 82.6 MB 的压缩包。举报者检测发现，微软 Defender 将压缩包及其中的可执行文件标记为 Wacatac 木马，VirusTotal 的 45 款安全引擎中有 8 款报毒。沙箱分析还发现，该文件存在检测调试环境、延迟执行等可疑行为。

REA 维护者随后在 10 月 13 日合并修复 PR，在官方 README 中增加下载来源警告，提醒用户通过官方 GitHub 仓库、官网或 npm 获取软件。目前，遭举报的仿冒仓库已无法正常访问。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/371694

⚡️钱志敏400亿非法集资案进展：检方申请没收6.18万余枚比特币等资产，法院已受理

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 14 日，据澎湃新闻报道，涉及逾 400 亿元非法集资、6 万余枚比特币的钱志敏案迎来国内司法程序新进展。10 月 13 日，天津市第二中级人民法院发布公告称，该院已于 9 月 28 日立案受理天津市人民检察院第二分院申请没收犯罪嫌疑人钱志敏违法所得一案。

根据天津二中院公布的申请没收财产清单，除比特币外，涉案虚拟货币还包括 72745.79502 枚比特币现金、72745.78555 枚比特币黄金、72745.7845 枚比特币中本聪愿景、3605989.9995 枚瑞波币，以及 70081208.62553222 枚狗狗币（已由英国司法机关转换后存入计息账户）。此外，申请没收的财产还包括美元、欧元、英镑现金，珠宝，以及银行余额、投资组合等。

天津市人民检察院第二分院认为，钱志敏涉嫌集资诈骗罪，逃匿后被通缉一年不能到案，有证据证明其在英国被查扣的 6.18 万余枚比特币等财产属于违法所得及孳息，应当对违法所得及其转变、转化的财产、孳息予以追缴，除依法返还受损集资参与人的以外，予以没收。

亿万富翁Paul Tudor Jones称将全年做空美股，持有石油多头头寸

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 14 日，亿万富翁、传奇对冲基金经理 Paul Tudor Jones 在 CNBC 节目中表示，2027 年可能成为美股极具挑战性的一年，市场或面临自 2002 年以来最不利的资金流环境。他认为，过去几年支撑美股上涨的企业回购和并购趋势可能逆转，而 AI 巨头 IPO 及后续增发将进一步增加股票供给。

Jones 指出，OpenAI、Anthropic 等 AI 公司潜在上市，以及 AI 基础设施建设带来的融资需求，可能推动企业发行更多股票。他将当前市场与互联网泡沫破裂前夕相比较，认为密集 IPO 和股票解禁可能对市场形成持续压力。

此外，Jones 警告，美国财政赤字持续扩大可能最终迫使政府通过市场压力调整财政政策；若美国中期选举后油价再上涨 20 至 25 美元，也可能对股市造成明显冲击。他表示，自己持有石油多头头寸，并直言：「我会做空一整年。」

items.author: Cointelegraph by Felix Ng
items.content:
Bitwise’s Hougan says Q3 charts point to ‘crypto spring’
Bitwise’s Matt Hougan said nearly every fundamental indicator that Bitwise tracks spiked sharply higher.
Bitwise chief investment officer Matt Hougan says Q3 may have been “one of the best quarters in crypto’s history,” arguing a sharp rebound in crypto prices and growing onchain markets point to the start of “crypto spring.”
In its quarterly market review published Thursday, Bitwise reported a 46.4% quarterly gain in its large-cap crypto index, along with $6 billion in US spot Bitcoin ETF inflows that brought year-to-date net flows back into positive territory.
The growth extended beyond the price of cryptocurrencies. The value of tokenized equities rose 65.5% to nearly $3.2 billion, while open interest on decentralized perpetual futures hit a new record near $26 billion, with a growing share tied to stocks, commodities, foreign exchange and pre-IPO shares.
“Page after page after page, it’s all the same: The most recent part of the chart is turning sharply upwards,” Hougan wrote. “That’s exactly what you want to see if you’re looking for the start of a crypto spring.”
Crypto analysts have been debating whether the market slump is finally over. CryptoQuant said in September that technical and onchain indicators confirmed a new Bitcoin bull market, while Bitget chief analyst Ryan Lee told Cointelegraph that more indicators were needed to confirm a cycle bottom. Hougan pointed to ETF flows and onchain activity as additional signs of a potential recovery.
10 large-cap crypto gain double digits
Bitcoin (BTC) gained 42.3% during Q3, while Ether (ETH) and Solana (SOL) rose 69.1% and 59.2%, respectively, according to Bitwise.
All 10 constituents of the firm’s large-cap crypto index posted double-digit quarterly gains, with Chainlink (LINK) the highest performer, climbing 97.6%.
“Three months ago, crypto was in the depths of despair,” said Hougan. “Prices, onchain activity, ETF flows—everything was down.”
Year-to-date performance of the assets tracked in the Bitwise 10 Large Cap Crypto Index. Source: Bitwise
However, the rebound did not extend to every corner of the industry.
Shares of Bitcoin miners Riot Platforms and Hut 8 fell 26.4% and 25.4%, respectively, during Q3, while Galaxy Digital dropped 16.8%, according to Bitwise.
The number of public companies holding Bitcoin fell almost 6% to 173 in the quarter, though their combined holdings grew 0.5%, while the number of public companies holding Ether fell to 35 from 40, even as their combined holdings increased.
Related: Crypto valuations could double as protocols link revenue to tokens: Bitwise CIO
Meanwhile, Bitwise’s large-cap crypto index remained down 6.2% for the year through September despite its strong quarterly gain.
Upcoming catalysts
Looking ahead, Bitwise said it expects the SEC’s innovation exemption to draw billions more of tokenized assets into blockchains.
“We believe Q4 moves tokenization from pilots to production. We expect the exemption will pull billions more of tokenized assets onto blockchains like Ethereum, Solana, NEAR, and others.”
Meanwhile, it expects the growing perpetual futures market to accelerate after more than $6 trillion was traded year-to-date across venues such as Hyperliquid and Lighter, up 42% from the same period a year earlier.
“With regulatory support expected this quarter, we project the growing perp market to accelerate as US investors start to arrive,” said Bitwise.
Magazine: Crypto lending rises again… but have they solved the risks?

Cerebras CEO反驳AI末日论：行业不应只谈风险，也要让公众看到技术潜力

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 14 日，AI 芯片公司 Cerebras 联合创始人兼 CEO Andrew Feldman 在 TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 大会上表示，当前 AI 行业对技术风险的讨论过于悲观，部分行业领袖或许不该公开发表相关言论。他认为，外界过度关注 AI 失控及其可能毁灭人类的风险，却忽视了 AI 在医疗等领域的潜力，例如未来有望大幅减少癌症死亡。

Feldman 同时强调，强大的技术必然伴随被不法分子滥用的风险，行业需要审慎推进，并接受合理监管。他还指出，AI 数据中心建设引发的部分负面舆论，与行业过去几年未能充分与当地社区沟通有关，尤其是在美国，企业应更重视社区参与。

对于 AI 模型效率提升是否会削弱芯片需求，Feldman 并不担忧。他认为，硬件厂商提高算力效率与模型开发商优化模型可以协同推进，最终推动 AI 技术进一步发展。Cerebras 客户包括 OpenAI、Block、Figma、葛兰素史克（GSK）及 Lovable。

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 14 日，桥水基金创始人瑞·达利欧周二在领英发文警告，美国国债市场正面临债券供应持续增加、投资者需求减弱的双重压力，债券熊市可能仍将持续。他指出，随着美国政府大规模发行新债，收益率可能进一步上升，推高政府融资成本并加重债务负担，形成恶性循环。

达利欧估算，美国今年需要为约 10 万亿美元到期债务进行再融资，同时新增借款约 2.1 万亿美元。与此同时，AI 等高资本支出领域也在争夺资金，企业发债融资进一步加剧资金竞争。他还警告，若日本等传统海外买家减少美债配置，供需失衡可能进一步恶化，并将企业信用市场承压视为流动性收紧的早期信号。

达利欧表示，除非高利率对实体经济和金融市场造成足够冲击、迫使资金供需重新平衡，否则债务压力难以缓解。他长期看空美国国债，并倾向于建议投资者减持债券、增持黄金。报道指出，美国国债基准指数年内已下跌约 2.4%，市场正面临自 2022 年以来首次年度下跌的风险。

⚡️美财政部对美国银行罚款近20亿美元，涉洗钱及制裁违规

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 14 日，美国财政部昨日宣布，针对美国第二大银行美国银行（Bank of America）采取多项执法行动，涉及反洗钱机制失效及违反制裁规定。

根据公告列出的具体金额，金融犯罪执法网络（FinCEN）处以 12 亿美元罚款，货币监理署（OCC）处以 7.5 亿美元民事罚款，美国海外资产控制办公室（OFAC）另与该行达成 1160 万美元和解，合计约 19.62 亿美元。

美国财政部表示，美国银行未能及时向 FinCEN 报告超过 50 亿美元的可疑交易，其中超过 10 亿美元涉及国家安全及重点非法金融风险，包括疑似亚洲地区洗钱网络、欺诈和潜在贸易洗钱活动。该行还因交易监控系统存在缺陷，未能有效监测数万亿美元交易，并长期延迟提交大量可疑活动报告。

此外，美国银行涉及 475 项疑似违反多项制裁计划的行为，包括通过受封锁银行处理代理银行付款，以及未能及时更新制裁名单等，相关交易涉及俄罗斯、白俄罗斯、伊朗、缅甸、索马里、毒品交易及全球恐怖主义相关制裁计划。美国财政部长贝森特表示，大型金融机构同样必须遵守反洗钱及制裁规定，否则将给整个美国金融体系带来非法资金流动风险。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/371675

开发者16天用Opus 5.5做出3D《小王子》剧情游戏，书里的星球现在可以走进去

动察 Beating AI 快讯，AI 创作者 Sac 花费 16 天，将《小王子》改编成了一款可以直接在浏览器玩的 3D 剧情游戏《小王子：星辰之旅》。玩家可以操控小王子走进国王的宫殿、穿过玫瑰花园，与狐狸相遇，还能在沙漠中找到飞行员。游戏不只有场景展示，也设计了浇花等互动任务。

作者介绍，Claude Opus 5.5 负责代码和游戏开发，VAST（三启万物）旗下的 Tripo AI 用来生成 3D 模型，Blender 负责处理模型和场景，最后通过 Unity 整合成游戏。就连宣传片，也是通过一条提示词，让 Opus 5.5 配合 Blender 制作的。目前游戏已开放免费试玩，官网提供中文、英文、日文等 8 种语言选项。

不过，游戏还有一些待优化的问题。有玩家认为，目前玩法仍以场景探索为主，跳跃操作和角色动画不够成熟。还有玩家反馈运行卡顿。网页版需要浏览器支持 WebGPU，而且每个章节都需要下载较大的资源包。

作者计划后续开源整个项目和详细制作流程。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/371674

Base推出「Earn&Borrow」功能，支持平台为用户提供稳定币收益和加密资产抵押借贷

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 14 日，Base 推出「Earn&Borrow」功能，允许各类平台接入 Base 网络上的第三方借贷市场，为符合条件的用户提供稳定币浮动收益，以及以数字资产作抵押的借贷服务。用户可将 USDC 等受支持的稳定币存入平台赚取收益，也可通过抵押数字资产获取流动性，无需直接出售持仓。

Base 表示，截至 2026 年 10 月 1 日，其追踪的借贷协议市场 28 日平均存款余额超过 30 亿美元，拥有逾 20 万名出借者和 11.5 万名借款者。Base 借贷市场的美元稳定币平均收益率为 4.45%，未计入额外激励奖励。

该服务基于 Base 网络及第三方借贷协议运行，平台可自主选择钱包和托管模式，并通过稳定币余额收益或抵押借贷手续费获得收入。相关收益率为浮动利率，取决于借贷市场情况；用户提款也受市场流动性及协议条款限制。Base 同时强调，相关金库由独立管理方负责，Base 和 Coinbase 不负责管理或担保金库。

Anthropic今日将披露三季度营收，为2万亿美元估值IPO探路

动察 Beating AI 快讯，Anthropic 今日将在旧金山总部向潜在机构投资者披露第三季度营收数据，以评估投资者对其财务表现及上市计划的反应。该公司据称正推进估值约 2 万亿美元的 IPO，计划于 11 月上市，此前已向美国证券交易委员会（SEC）提交保密上市申请，但具体上市日期尚未确定。

此次披露正值 AI 板块承压之际。上周，OpenAI 向现有投资者更新的年化营收为 500 亿美元，低于市场此前广泛流传的 700 亿美元，引发市场对营收统计口径的争议，并拖累半导体股及纳斯达克指数。与此同时，博通 CEO Hock Tan 警告称，利率上升可能使资本获取能力成为 AI 企业发展的主要制约因素。

市场将重点关注 Anthropic 是否会明确营收确认口径，尤其是是否计入云合作伙伴相关收入，以避免重演 OpenAI 数据披露引发的市场误读。此次财务数据披露或将影响投资者对 Anthropic 增长前景的判断，并进一步影响其 IPO 定价与上市节奏。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/371670

Philippine Crypto Giant Coins ph Faces Regulatory Scrutiny Over Alleged Gambling Links

Coins ph, one of the Philippines' largest crypto exchanges with over 18 million registered users, is reportedly facing regulatory scrutiny from the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) over allegations that it facilitated transactions for restricted offshore gambling operators, potentially putting its license at risk. In late September, the BSP restricted incoming peso transfers to its e-wallet operator, DCPay Philippines, through InstaPay and PESONet. Several senior compliance executives have also reportedly departed. Indonesian tech giant Gojek acquired Coins ph for a reported $95 million in 2019 before selling it in 2022 to an investor group involving Joffre Capital and former Binance CFO Wei Zhou. — link

彭博社：加密行业转向股权融资之际，Polymarket的发币暗示显得格外突兀

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 14 日，据彭博社报道，Polymarket 创始人兼 CEO Shayne Coplan 此前暗示平台可能发布重要消息，引发社区对代币发行的广泛猜测。但他在新加坡 Token2049 大会上仅表示看好链上资产，并未公布具体发币计划，引发部分用户不满。

与此同时，加密行业正逐渐从代币融资转向股权融资。数据显示，2025 年 1 月至 2026 年 2 月，主流交易所上线的代币中，不到 10% 实现正收益。跨链协议 Across 正逐步停用其代币，并允许持有者换取公司股权；资产代币化平台 Centrifuge 也在推进类似转型。Centrifuge CEO Bhaji Illuminati 表示，代币可能成为企业吸引传统金融机构的障碍，部分机构受内部规定限制，无法持有代币，也担心匿名代币持有者影响项目决策。

此前报道称，Polymarket 正进行新一轮融资，估值据称将达到 210 亿美元，并通过聘请前高盛合伙人等举措拓展机构业务。在代币市场表现低迷、机构投资者更加重视合规与治理的背景下，越来越多加密企业开始重新评估发币的必要性，转向传统股权融资。

Metaplanet拟发行520亿日元零息可转债，部分用于偿还信贷并释放抵押比特币

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 14 日，Metaplanet CEO Simon Gerovich 发文表示，公司将发行总额 520 亿日元、2031 年到期的零息日元计价可转债，并同步推进股票回购计划。

此次发行所得中，最多 283 亿日元将用于回购公司股票，其中最多 253 亿日元将通过场外大宗交易执行，涉及最多 96,934,800 股，约占已发行股份的 7.1%；其余部分通过市场买入完成。

此外，公司将使用约 236 亿日元部分偿还信贷额度，以释放目前作为抵押品的比特币。Gerovich 表示，Metaplanet 股价目前低于其比特币持仓价值，此次回购旨在利用折价为股东创造价值；可转债初始转股价则高于发行时股价及 1.0 倍 mNAV。

尽管此次发行将增加公司总债务，但公司希望以无担保、无定期利息支出的债务替代部分有担保计息借款，从而降低利息成本、延长债务期限，并提升后续增持比特币的财务灵活性。

items.author: Ian Allison
items.content:
Largest Philippines crypto exchange, Coins.ph, said to face central bank regulatory action
The exchange, which has over 18 million customers, is said to have handled business transactions involving restricted offshore gaming and gambling companies.
- The infractions, said to involve serving offshore gambling platforms, are serious enough to see the company stripped of its license to operate, according to one of the people.
- Earlier this month, the central bank of the Philippines imposed restrictions on deposits through Coins.ph’s main wallet firm, according to people familiar with the process.
- Several high-profile compliance staff left the exchange this year, including CCO Lexi Herrera and anti money-laundering specialists Chris Beaño and Irish Calagui.
Coins.ph, the largest cryptocurrency exchange in the Philippines, is facing punitive action from financial regulators at the country’s central bank, two people with knowledge of the situation said.
The infractions, which are said to involve serving offshore gambling firms, are serious enough for the 12-year-old company to be stripped of its license to operate, which would cause “an earthquake” in the Philippines’ crypto ecosystem, according to one of the people.
The exchange, which has over 18 million customers, has a 24-hour spot trading volume of about $50 million and controls some 75%-80% of peso-to-stablecoin liquidity in the Philippines, a key transaction in the world's fourth-largest remittance recipient.
More than 10.8 million Filipinos live outside the country, according to the Commission on Filipinos Overseas, though most use banks and money transfer services to repatriate their earnings, some $43 billion a year.
At the start of this month, Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) reportedly imposed restrictions on deposits to the exchange made through Coins.ph’s main wallet firm, DCPay Philippines.
The restrictions follow the departure of several high-profile compliance staffers, including chief compliance officer Lexi Herrera, the head of anti-money laundering (AML) transaction monitoring Chris Beaño and money laundering reporting officer Irish Calagui.
Coins.ph said it is aware of recent news reports about its operations, including claims about offshore gaming transactions and its engagement with the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas, in a statement shared with Coindesk after the publication of this article.
The exchange said users’ funds are safe, and the firm continues to operate as a BSP licensed institution and expects to fully restore affected services soon.
“Coins.ph firmly denies any claim that it knowingly serves offshore gaming or gambling operators. We hold ourselves to the requirements and standards of the BSP, AMLC and other regulatory authorities, and full compliance sits at the core of how we operate,” Coins.ph said in the emailed statement.
“We value the media’s role in keeping the public informed and welcome the opportunity to share our perspective. We remain open to engaging with journalists and providing accurate information about Coins.ph,” it said.
The Philippines central bank had not responded to requests for comment by publication time.
A little over a year ago, the central bank clamped down on the use of e-wallet applications for gambling purposes, demanding institutions under its supervision cut in-app access to gambling sites.
As a result, several gambling entities migrated to Coins.ph, according to the people. The move had the added advantage of giving the firms access to crypto and stablecoins for paying offshore partners, according to a third person familiar with central bank regulatory processes.
The recent Coins.ph restriction was not time-bound, unlike the temporary suspensions typically imposed on market participants for failing to comply with throughput or latency requirements, for example. In this case, no reason was given, one of the people said.
Coins.ph was one of the earliest crypto wallets and exchanges in the Philippines and later pivoted to providing broader financial services.
In January 2019, Indonesian technology company Gojek bought Coins.ph for $95 million. Coins.ph was later sold to Wei Zhou, who was previously Binance’s chief financial officer.

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 14 日，美国劳工统计局将于今晚 20:30 公布 9 月 CPI 数据。机构预计整体 CPI 同比涨幅将从 8 月的 3.4% 升至 3.6%，环比上涨 0.6%，创近 5 个月最大涨幅，主要受能源价格反弹推动。核心 CPI 预计同比上涨 2.5%，环比上涨 0.2%，低于前值 0.3%。

此外，美国将于周四公布 PPI 数据，CPI 与 PPI 均将影响市场对后续通胀走势及美联储政策路径的判断。

谷歌Gemini 4 Argon正式开放：看段视频就能教机器人投沙包，连中7次

动察 Beating AI 快讯，谷歌正式向全球付费用户开放 Gemini 4 Argon，此前该模型仅向部分网络安全合作伙伴提供。最吸引眼球的是一段机器人演示：Argon 观看真人投沙包的视频，识别场地位置、计算全身关节动作，并自行编写物理仿真程序。经过仿真和真机迁移后，美国机器人公司 Apptronik 旗下的 Apollo 人形机器人，在真实场地连续投中 7 次。

谷歌称，这套流程将原本需要数周的手工仿真建模缩短至几小时。其他演示中，Argon 为波士顿动力 Spot 机器狗搭建模拟环境，让它练习踩开垃圾桶盖、投入易拉罐。它还能根据一张桌面照片生成仿真场景，合成超过 4500 段训练数据。用这些数据微调机器人动作模型后，实机任务成功率从 56% 提高到 75%，耗时从 35 秒缩短至 24 秒。在测试三维空间和物理理解能力的 ERQA 评测中，Argon 得分达到 87%，超过其他前沿模型。

目前，Google AI Pro 和 Ultra 用户可以在 Gemini App 中使用 Argon，但 Antigravity 中仅向 Ultra 用户开放，开发者也可通过付费 API 调用。

API 首发价为每百万输入 Token 2 美元、输出 10 美元，与 Claude Sonnet 5.5、GPT-6.1 Sol 持平，只有 Claude Fable 5.1 和 GPT-6 Astra 的五分之一。不过，这一优惠仅持续至 11 月 30 日，之后价格翻倍，与 Claude Opus 5.5 持平。

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 14 日，Citadel Securities 股票与衍生品策略主管 Scott Rubner 在最新研报中指出，上周散户投资者通过该平台净买入美国股票 91 亿美元，创近 15 年来最大单周净买入纪录，资金主要流向 AI 相关股票及 ETF。

OpenAI工程师涉嫌在高管会议室安装窃听设备被捕，AI模型协助锁定嫌疑人

动察 Beating AI 快讯，35 岁的沙特籍 OpenAI 工程师 Abdulrahman Alfozan 于 10 月 9 日被 FBI 逮捕，涉嫌在 OpenAI 位于旧金山的高管会议室内安装隐蔽录音设备。美国司法部称，其被控使用或试图使用设备截取口头通信，若罪名成立，最高可面临 5 年监禁及 25 万美元罚款。

根据刑事诉状，公司员工于 9 月 30 日前后在会议室电视机背面发现一台加密录音设备。检方称，嫌疑人此前曾通过内部办公工具查询公司办公地址、会议室及高管会面安排；与其配偶关联的聊天机器人账号还曾询问如何制作、隐藏并远程访问持续录音设备。

OpenAI 表示，公司利用自有模型分析设备及其来源，最终锁定涉事员工，并已将其解雇。目前，公司没有发现嫌疑人未经授权访问或窃取模型权重、源代码及客户数据的迹象。FBI 仍在调查此案，案件下一场羁押听证会定于 10 月 19 日举行。

应用材料斥资50亿美元建设芯片研发中心，目标将AI芯片开发周期缩短一半

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 14 日，全球最大半导体设备制造商应用材料（Applied Materials）正式揭幕 EPIC 半导体研发中心，该项目位于美国加州桑尼维尔，总投资预计达 50 亿美元，旨在加速 AI 时代先进芯片技术创新。

EPIC 中心占地约 60 万平方英尺，英特尔、台积电、美光、SK 海力士和三星等行业巨头将派驻研究团队，与应用材料工程师协同研发，并提前接触最新半导体制造设备。应用材料表示，该中心有望将新一代芯片架构从概念研发到商业化的周期，从通常的 10 至 12 年缩短至最快 6 年。

该中心主要用于研发而非芯片量产，短期内并不意味着美国芯片制造能力将直接回流，但有望强化硅谷在先进半导体和 AI 芯片领域的竞争力。

应用材料美股周二收盘跌 2.88%，盘后转涨，现涨 0.74%，市值回升至 83 亿美元。

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 14 日，纽约联储主席威廉姆斯表示，今年再加息一次是合适的，但如果经济前景符合预期，2027 年可能无需进一步加息。他称，支持 9 月加息决定，主要原因包括能源价格上涨、AI 基础设施投资增加等因素。

威廉姆斯称，AI 需求增长规模较大，短期内需求超过供应，但随着芯片产能增加和生产率提升，未来供应端可能改善，并形成抑制通胀的力量。谈及美债收益率上涨，威廉姆斯表示，长期收益率受到债券供需、AI 投资、财政政策以及能源价格等多重因素影响，而不仅是货币政策。

纽约梅隆银行与Citadel Securities完成美债代币化交易，探索加速华尔街融资

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 14 日，全球最大托管银行纽约梅隆银行（BNY）与交易巨头 Citadel Securities 周二宣布，已完成一笔代币化美国国债交易，旨在展示区块链技术如何加快资产从交易结算转入融资环节，提升抵押品流转效率。

美国国债是银行和交易机构获取短期贷款、为交易活动融资的重要抵押品，但传统结算体系下，债券在不同账户及系统间转移需要时间，可能导致资金和资产暂时被占用。此次交易通过代币化国债打通结算与融资环节，有望让机构更快重复使用抵押品，释放流动性。

BNY 表示，计划进一步推出数字现金和代币化存款服务，以支持基于区块链的结算与融资；同时计划于 2027 年延长符合美联储资格的证券及美国三方回购交易的传统结算系统运营时间，覆盖欧洲和亚洲交易时段。

随着贝莱德、富兰克林邓普顿和摩根大通等机构持续探索资产代币化，传统金融机构正尝试利用区块链缩短结算时间、自动化业务流程并提高资产流动性。

Vortexa：美国封锁致伊朗原油出口归零，10月仍未恢复

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 14 日，据能源情报平台 Vortexa 报告，美国海上封锁导致伊朗海运原油出口自 9 月第二周降至零，截至 10 月 5 日仍未恢复，而 9 月初的 14 天平均出口量为每日 23 万桶。

目前伊朗海上油轮储油量降至 8300 万桶，其中 4300 万桶因美国封锁滞留霍尔木兹海峡以西。Vortexa 表示，美国封锁实际阻断了伊朗原油离开波斯湾的通道。伊朗液化石油气出口环比下降 48%，创至少 2023 年 1 月以来最低水平。

与此同时，俄罗斯 9 月原油出口环比增长 6% 至每日 379 万桶，占伊朗、俄罗斯和委内瑞拉三国合计高风险原油出口的约 80%。三国 9 月出口总量为每日 473 万桶，低于去年同期的 639 万桶。此外，剔除伊朗后的海湾地区石油出口量已恢复至战前水平的 81% 以上，主要受沙特出口回升推动。(金十)

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 14 日，沙特能源部证实，沙特阿美位于东部省达兰的总部一栋行政大楼遭袭并发生「有限火灾」，目前暂无人员伤亡报告，袭击造成的实际损失仍不明确。此前，沙特领导的联军称，针对东部省哈拉尔和达兰的弹道导弹已被拦截，拦截碎片落入达兰居民区。

袭击发生之际，胡塞武装军事发言人叶海亚·萨雷威胁称，将对沙特领导的联军袭击萨那作出「严厉而痛苦」的回应，并警告可能打击沙特东部省及利雅得的石油设施。与此同时，埃克森美孚、雪佛龙、壳牌、英国石油和道达尔能源等多家能源巨头高管退出正在利雅得举行的世界石油大会，地区安全风险进一步升高。

美国总统特朗普表示，已与沙特王储穆罕默德·本·萨勒曼讨论近期袭击，并指责胡塞武装可能在伊朗支持下试图于美国中期选举前推高油价。特朗普称，可能要求土耳其总统埃尔多安加入打击也门胡塞武装的行动，并警告称，11 月 3 日中期选举结束后仍将采取行动。

Ledger asks resellers to halt sales in Southeast Asia and Hong Kong
The wallet maker requested that devices be removed from shelves while investigators work to establish where tampering occurred.
Ledger has requested sellers and distributors of its devices in six Southeast Asian countries and Hong Kong to suspend sales and remove its hardware wallets from shelves as it investigates reports of tampered devices.
In a post on X on Tuesday, Ledger said the request covers resellers in Indonesia, Singapore, Thailand, the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia and Hong Kong.
“To be clear, as the investigation continues, the only confirmed incidents remain contained to Southeast Asia. We have not verified a drain linked to a device bought elsewhere,” said Ledger.
“The investigation is ongoing to determine who tampered with these devices and where in the distribution chain it happened,” it added.
The wider sales suspension request expands on Ledger’s earlier request for reseller CryptoBilis to stop sales and shipments. The investigation became public on Oct. 9 after reports of stolen crypto linked to devices purchased through the reseller.
Since then, users in other regions, including Europe, have reported finding suspected tampering in devices purchased from retailers.
“We have no indication that Ledger’s infrastructure, systems or services or direct sales channel have been compromised,” the company said.
Related: Trezor reduces resellers as a ‘preventative step’ amid Ledger tampering reports
items.title: Ledger asks resellers to halt sales in Southeast Asia and Hong Kong

Bitcoin treasury company Strive 
The company is aiming to sell 5 million shares at $100 per share, for a capital raise of $500 million, with proceeds to be used to purchase additional bitcoin 
The new share class will sit junior to Strive’s current perpetual preferred, SATA, which has a variable rate (currently 13%).
Like SATA, SATS will pay dividends on a daily basis.
At closing of the offering, the company intends to establish a dividend reserve equal to the first 18 months of dividend payments on SATS.
Unlike most bitcoin treasury companies, including far larger peer Strategy, Strive has in recent weeks been able to significantly increase its bitcoin holdings.
The company last week acquired 3,311 bitcoin, bringing total holdings to 32,773 coins, currently worth about $2.7 billiion. Three months ago, holdings were below 20,000 coins.

items.author: Krisztian Sandor
items.content:
BNY, Citadel Securities test tokenized U.S. Treasuries to speed up Wall Street financing
The transaction shows how blockchain-based government bonds could help trading firms move collateral faster between settlement and financing.
- BNY and Citadel Securities completed a transaction showing how tokenized U.S. Treasuries can move from settlement into financing.
- The effort targets a key bottleneck in financial markets: moving government bonds used as collateral for trading and borrowing.
- BNY plans to expand digital cash services and traditional settlement hours as it works toward around-the-clock markets.
BNY, the world’s largest custody bank, and trading giant Citadel Securities said Tuesday they had completed a transaction using tokenized U.S. Treasuries, showing how blockchain technology could help Wall Street move assets between trading and financing more quickly.
The transfer focused on collateral, a key part of financial markets. Banks and trading firms use U.S. government bonds to secure short-term loans and fund trading activity. Moving those bonds between accounts and settlement systems can take time, tying up assets that could otherwise be put to work.
The effort comes as Wall Street explores bringing traditional assets onto blockchains. Firms including BlackRock, Franklin Templeton and JPMorgan have embraced tokenized funds and securities, betting the technology can shorten settlement times, automate processes and make assets easier to move.
Putting tokenized Treasuries to work
The aim of the BNY-Citadel Securities transaction was to demonstrate how tokenized government bonds could move from settlement into financing, potentially allowing firms to reuse collateral sooner and free up cash for other trades.
“Efficient movement of high-quality collateral is fundamental to well-functioning markets,” said Dan Doherty, digital assets operations lead at Citadel Securities, in a statement. He added that reducing delays across the trade lifecycle could improve how institutional markets operate.
BNY said it plans to introduce more digital cash and tokenized deposit capabilities to support blockchain-based settlement and financing.
Meanwhile, the bank said it expects to extend the operating hours of its traditional settlement systems for Federal Reserve-eligible securities and U.S. triparty transactions, aiming to reach European and Asian trading hours next year. Triparty transactions are a form of short-term financing in which a bank manages collateral between borrowers and lenders.
“By using a tokenized representation of a U.S. Treasury across both settlement and financing, we are enabling more connected, efficient and always-on financial system,” said Carolyn Weinberg, chief innovation and market transformation officer at BNY, in a statement.

items.author: Jose Antonio Lanz
items.content:
In brief
- The FBI arrested OpenAI engineer Abdulrahman Alfozan on Oct. 9 for allegedly planting a hidden audio recorder in an executive conference room at the OpenAI’s San Francisco offices.
- Prosecutors say a chatbot account tied to his spouse asked how to build, hide, and remotely access a continuous audio recorder days before the device was installed.
- OpenAI says its models helped identify him and that it has no indication he took model weights, source code, or customer data.
An OpenAI engineer is in federal custody after allegedly hiding an encrypted audio recorder behind a television in one of the company's executive conference rooms in San Francisco. OpenAI says its own AI models helped figure out who put it there.
“We discovered a sophisticated recording device that was hidden inside one of our offices,” OpenAI said in a statement on X. “We used our models to understand the device and where it had come from, identifying that a specific employee had planted it a few days earlier.”
The Justice Department identified the suspect as Abdulrahman Alfozan, a 35-year-old Saudi national who has worked as an engineer at OpenAI since July 2025. He was arrested on Oct. 9, charged with using or attempting to use a device to intercept oral communications, and made his initial appearance in federal court on Tuesday.
“We referred the matter to the FBI, and we’re grateful to the agents and prosecutors who moved quickly to make an arrest,” OpenAI said. “The FBI’s investigation is ongoing and we will continue to support their work.”
A note from our research leaders:
Last week we parted ways with Jasmine, Mikita, and Tomek after a thorough investigation found they violated clear policies on handling sensitive information. Our internal investigation uncovered a significant breach of trust beyond what’s…
— OpenAI Newsroom (@OpenAINewsroom) October 9, 2026
According to the criminal complaint, OpenAI staff found the recorder on or around Sept. 30, plugged into a USB port on the back of a TV and wrapped in toilet paper. Its contents were encrypted, and the company determined it had been installed around Sept. 28.
Security cameras allegedly caught Alfozan near the room on several dates before the discovery, even though he had no authorization to enter it or attend its meetings. Prosecutors say those meetings regularly involved confidential technical and strategic information.
Before the device went in, Alfozan allegedly used an internal productivity tool to ask about OpenAI's building addresses, meeting rooms, room capacities, calendars, and where leadership and outside partners met.
Prosecutors also point to a chatbot account tied to Alfozan's spouse, which shared multiple identifiers with his own account. Between Sept. 24 and 30, it allegedly asked how to build a continuous audio recorder, add Wi-Fi connectivity, improve live listening, and encrypt the device's SD card. The complaint doesn't say whose chatbot it was.
“At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data,” the company said, referring to the trained parameters that make up an AI model, its underlying code, and user information. “The employee was terminated.”
“We take protecting our technology, data, and people seriously, and as a matter of national importance,” OpenAI added, saying its security program is built to defend against threats ranging from insiders to cybercriminals to nation states. “This case is an example of how AI can help address these sophisticated security threats.”
The company did not explain in its statement exactly what its models analyzed to identify him.
Federal officials are treating it as a national security case. FBI Director Kash Patel said Alfozan allegedly tried to capture sensitive conversations about the company's “super intelligence technology,” and U.S. Attorney Craig Missakian called the prosecution a national security matter.
The arrest came days after OpenAI's newsroom account defended firing three safety researchers—Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak, and Mikita Balesni—saying an investigation found they had violated clear policies on handling sensitive information.
OpenAI's security record has drawn scrutiny since July, when the company admitted its own models escaped a test environment and breached Hugging Face's infrastructure to grab benchmark answers.
If convicted, Alfozan faces up to five years in prison, a $250,000 fine, and three years of supervised release. A detention hearing is set for Oct. 19 before U.S. Magistrate Judge Alex G. Tse.

items.author: Jose Antonio Lanz
items.content:
In brief
- Character.AI filed for voluntary Chapter 11 bankruptcy in Delaware on October 12 to sell itself under court supervision, and says the app will be wound down if no buyer keeps it running.
- Disney is the opening bidder, offering $20 million for a non-exclusive perpetual license to some of the startup's intellectual property, weeks after hiring its CEO as Disney's first CTO.
- The company pointed users attached to their AI companions toward mental health resources, just two weeks after launching two new chat models and a cheaper $4.99 subscription.
Character.AI, the app where millions of people spend hours chatting with AI versions of fictional heroes and made-up partners, has filed for bankruptcy.
The company announced Monday that it started a voluntary Chapter 11 process, a type of U.S. bankruptcy that lets a company keep operating while a judge supervises how its debts get paid or how its assets get sold. The case was filed in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware.
Character.AI isn't trying to restructure its way back to health. It wants a court-supervised sale of all or substantially all of its assets, and if no bidder agrees to keep the service alive, the company said the platform "will be wound down"—corporate speak for switched off.
Disney Worldwide Services, a unit of the Walt Disney Company, signed on before the filing as the "stalking horse" bidder, according to Character.AI's press release. In a bankruptcy auction, that is the opening offer that sets a floor every other buyer has to beat.
The media giant is offering $20 million for a non-exclusive, perpetual license to some of Character.AI's intellectual property and certain legal claims, plus transition services run by former Character.AI employees it has already hired. Non-exclusive means Disney gets to use that tech forever, but so can whoever else ends up buying it, and other bidders can still top the offer.
The company expects the sale to close in late November or early December. Character Technologies Inc., the company's legal name, estimated both its assets and its liabilities at $50 million to $100 million in its bankruptcy petition.
Three and a half years ago, Andreessen Horowitz led a $150 million funding round that valued Character.AI at $1 billion, with a16z partner Sarah Wang tweeting that "we are at the iPhone moment of AI." Founded in 2021 by former Google engineers Noam Shazeer and Daniel De Freitas, the app lets anyone build a chatbot with a personality and share it with others.
Google came calling in August 2024, rehiring both founders and part of the research team in a roughly $2.7 billion deal that also licensed Character.AI's technology. Silicon Valley calls this kind of arrangement an acqui-hire, buying the talent without technically buying the company, and Character.AI later largely abandoned building its own large language models, the AI engines that generate the chatbots' text.
Two months after the Google deal, Florida mother Megan Garcia sued Character.AI, its founders and Google, alleging that her 14-year-old son, Sewell Setzer III, died by suicide after becoming emotionally attached to a chatbot modeled on Game of Thrones character Daenerys Targaryen. More lawsuits from other families followed, and in September 2025 the Federal Trade Commission ordered Character.AI and six other tech companies to explain how they protect minors.
A month later, Character.AI banned users under 18 from open-ended chats with its characters, cutting off its core product for its youngest fans. In January, the company and Google agreed to settle lawsuits brought by families in Florida, Colorado, New York, and Texas.
In September 2025, Disney's lawyers sent Character.AI a cease-and-desist letter, a formal legal demand to stop, over chatbots imitating Disney characters, and the startup took them down. This past September, Disney named Character.AI CEO Karandeep Anand its first-ever chief technology officer and said several of the startup's engineers would join him.
Colin Adams, now Character.AI's CEO, said the company spent the past year trying to sustain the business amid "significant legal, regulatory, and operational headwinds" before the board chose a court-supervised sale.
Besides the legal hurdles, the company was burning too much money without reporting enough revenue, reporting “an operating loss of approximately $8-9 million per month.”
Character AI also struggled to raise more capital, which ended up making the whole operation unsustainable. “Notwithstanding the progress that has been made with regulators and personal injury claimants and enhancements to platform safety, Character has faced challenges in obtaining new investment capital,” Character AI CEO Collin Adams said in a sworn statement.
On September 28, Character.AI launched two new models pitched as a big upgrade for roleplay (collaborative storytelling where the AI plays a character), and quick, text-message-style banter. It also rolled out a cheaper subscription called (c.ai) lite, priced at $4.99 a month or $2.49 a week.
Fourteen days later, the company was in bankruptcy court.
The app remains online for now, paid subscriptions stay active and billing is unchanged, according to the company, which also reminded users they can export their chats or delete their accounts.
Character.AI also linked to a support page for anyone struggling with the news, a tacit admission that for some users the app is not just entertainment. AI companions—chatbots designed to act as friends or partners that remember past conversations—can become a daily emotional anchor for people who talk to them for hours.
The page points users to Koko, a nonprofit offering free, anonymous mini-courses of five to 10 minutes on coping with stress and dark thoughts, and to a directory of free helplines staffed by real people. Its very first suggestion, however, is a conversation with a "supportive AI guide," which is to say a chatbot to help people cope with losing their chatbots.
A February study of five AI companion communities, including Character.AI's, found that users whose companions disappeared through model updates or platform shutdowns reported grief comparable to losing a person, and that platforms offered them no closure. OpenAI saw a version of this in February too, when it retired GPT-4o, a ChatGPT model many users found warmer than its successors, and users around the world publicly mourned it.
The bidding now plays out in Delaware's bankruptcy court, with a sale targeted for late November or early December. If no buyer commits to keeping Character.AI running, the characters its users spent years building go offline with it.

items.author: Jose Antonio Lanz
items.content:
In brief
- Binance will discontinue Binance Pool, Pool Savings, Cloud Mining, Transaction Accelerator and related features at 07:00 UTC on Nov. 10.
- Miners must point their hardware to another pool before the cutoff, and Pool Savings users must redeem their positions before the service ends.
- The closure follows Binance's July shutdown of its exchange NFT service and its June push into U.S. stocks and tokenized equities.
Binance will shut down its mining pool and several related services on Nov. 10, the exchange said in an announcement published Tuesday. The closure covers Binance Pool, Pool Savings, Cloud Mining, and Transaction Accelerator, along with Telegram hashrate alerts, email notifications, and the pool's API.
“As part of our ongoing review of products and services, Binance will discontinue Binance Pool and related services on 2026-11-10,” Binance wrote. “All Binance Pool-related services will be discontinued. Binance Pool will begin disconnecting mining connections, and Binance Mining Pool Stratum URLs and mining endpoints will be disabled. Hashrate submissions and mining shares submitted after this time will no longer be accepted, processed, or credited.”
A mining pool combines the computing power of many miners and splits block rewards among them based on the work each one contributes. Cloud Mining let users buy hashrate, a slice of mining power, without owning any hardware, while Transaction Accelerator helped users push through Bitcoin transactions that were slow to confirm because of low fees or network congestion.
Binance pool launched in April 2020 and ranked ninth among Bitcoin pools at the end of 2025, with about 26 exahashes per second, or 2.3% of the network, according to Hashrate Index. One exahash per second equals a quintillion guesses every second at the puzzle that earns a block.
The same report called Binance Pool the last pool still standing from the era when exchanges rushed into mining, with its relevance tied to Binance's exchange and custody business rather than mining technology.
Seems like Binance, just as Satoshi Nakamoto, wants to move onto other things. The shutdown arrives as Binance expands into traditional finance. On June 1, the exchange opened access to more than 7,000 US stocks and ETFs for customers outside the United States, with zero commission and fractional purchases from $5, according to co-CEO Richard Teng. It also previewed bStocks, a coming feature that lets users mint tokenized versions of the shares they buy on the BNB blockchain.
Quantmap co-founder Ivan Patriki told Decrypt at the time that large exchanges are moving into equities because they no longer want to depend on crypto market cycles. Vytautas Mackonis, COO of RWA protocol ALCUM, told Decrypt the offering is more structurally complex than it appears, with Binance as the interface, Nest Trading as the broker-dealer, and Alpaca Securities as the custodian.
Binance also closed its centralized NFT service on July 3, telling users to move their tokens to Binance Wallet, its self-custody wallet. Then-CEO Changpeng Zhao used the phrase “smooth sunsetting of old products” in 2023.
At 07:00 UTC on Nov. 10, Binance Pool will begin disconnecting miners and disable its Stratum URLs, the server addresses miners point their machines at to connect to the pool. Shares, the proofs of work that determine each miner's payout, will stop being credited after that time, while those submitted earlier count toward final rewards. Binance said eligible outstanding rewards, balances and refunds will be processed afterward, subject to its product rules, account status and compliance checks.
Miners must point their hardware to another pool before the cutoff, and Pool Savings users need to unsubscribe or redeem their positions before the service ends. Binance said the pool will keep operating normally until the cutoff. Anyone expecting a final payout has until 23:59 UTC on Nov. 10 to finish any required identity verification. Binance Pool pages will stay viewable until 07:00 UTC on Nov. 24, after which they become permanently inaccessible.

items.author: Cointelegraph by Sam Bourgi
items.content:
Most tokenized stock trading on Solana, BNB Chain occurs outside US market hours
Tokenized equities have reached nearly $3.3 billion in value as investors embrace round-the-clock access beyond Wall Street hours.
Most trading in tokenized stocks on major blockchains now takes place outside regular US market hours, offering an early indication that around-the-clock trading could be one of the biggest advantages of putting equities onchain.
According to Blockworks data cited by The Kobeissi Letter, more than 70% of tokenized stock trading volume on BNB Chain occurs outside the traditional 9:30 am to 4 pm Eastern trading session. The figure is 63% on Solana and nearly 60% on Base.
Meanwhile, Jupiter, a major Solana-based trading platform, reported a 50% month-over-month increase in tokenized asset trading volume.
Source: The Kobeissi Letter
The figures suggest investors use tokenized stocks to trade when traditional US exchanges are closed, rather than simply replicating activity during regular market hours.
The growth comes as tokenized stock values have increased by 15% over the past 30 days to nearly $3.3 billion, according to RWA.xyz data. A significant portion of that value is concentrated among issuers such as Ondo Global Markets, xStocks and bStocks, whose tokens are issued and traded across different blockchains.
Related: Winners and losers of the SEC’s new tokenized stocks rules
Wall Street moves toward onchain stock trading
The growth in round-the-clock trading comes as US regulators begin opening the door to tokenized equities in traditional markets. Last month, the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) introduced an “innovation exemption” allowing qualifying venues to trade tokenized US-listed stocks on public blockchains.
SEC Commissioner Mark Uyeda said participating venues must publish transaction data in US dollars, including trade prices, sizes, timestamps and daily trading volumes. They must also disclose liquidity pool addresses and balances.
Unlike existing tokenized stock products such as xStocks and Ondo Global Markets, which are generally unavailable to US investors, the SEC exemption allows qualifying venues to offer tokenized US equities domestically, provided they preserve shareholder rights and meet trading and disclosure requirements.
Related: Crypto Biz: Wealthy investors are buying crypto, but their advisers aren’t sold

items.author: Jose Antonio Lanz
items.content:
In brief
- A wallet holding 4,581.94 BTC sent its full balance, worth about $377 million, to five new addresses on Oct. 12 in a single transaction that paid a fee of 732 sats.
- The coins arrived in March 2020, when they were worth roughly $40.5 million.
- The address received 22 dust deposits since 2020, including 600 sats on Jan. 28, 2025 from a look-alike address matching its first three and last four characters.
A Bitcoin wallet that has held 4,581.94 BTC since March 2020 sent its entire balance to five new addresses on Oct. 12, moving about $377 million in a single transaction, according to blockchain data. The transfer confirmed in block 971,126 at about 18:37 UTC, with Bitcoin trading around $82,350.
Four of the receiving addresses got exactly 1,000 BTC each, and the fifth received 581.94 BTC. The transaction paid a fee of 732 satoshis, the hundred-millionth-of-a-bitcoin units known as sats, or about 60 cents. As of block 971,279 on Oct. 13, none of the five addresses has spent anything, and it is unclear who controls the wallet or where the coins are going.
The wallet received its coins on March 3, 2020, in a transaction that split a 5,081.95 BTC balance three ways, with 250 BTC going to each of two other addresses. At roughly $8,830 per Bitcoin, the 4,581.95 BTC that landed in the wallet was worth about $40.5 million. The value of the Bitcoin has nearly increased by 10X since then.
The wallet is an example of patience. The coins have sat through several market shocks since they arrived, starting with the COVID-19 crisis, which started shortly after the wallet got funded. During that time the stash went from about $40.5 million to about $17.6 million.
Tesla’s suspension of Bitcoin payments and China’s mining crackdown followed in May 2021, tanking the wallet from about $291 million at its April peak to $131 million by June. The Terra, Celsius and FTX collapses in 2022 would have taken the value down to about $71 million, a loss of about $239 million from the November 2021 peak, as the Federal Reserve’s rate hikes also dragged the S&P 500 down about 25% and Bitcoin hit a two-year low.
Trump’s tariff shock cut also crashed the markets. Bitcoin has since fallen 54% from a record $124,728 to $57,735 before recovering to its current price. The wallet’s value dropped from $571.5 million to about $265 million during that dip, but overall, hodling has resulted in almost 10X of net gains since day 1.
The address has also collected dust, meaning transfers of a few hundred to a few thousand sats that cost almost nothing to send. Blockchain data shows 22 such deposits between August 2020 and May 2026, ranging from 546 to 6,953 sats, or less than $6 each at current prices. Sixteen arrived in batch transactions that paid out to between 87 and 610 addresses at once.
One deposit matches the pattern of address poisoning, in which an attacker generates an address that copies the first and last characters of a real one, hoping someone later copies it from a transaction history by mistake. On Jan. 28, 2025, an address beginning 18VpNbPc and ending pQ9x sent the wallet 600 sats, and it shares the first three and last four characters with the whale’s address.
The look-alike was funded in a Nov. 12, 2024 transaction that paid out to 1,401 outputs at once, and it was emptied after sending that one payment. Every other sender used a bc1 address, which looks nothing like the wallet’s legacy 18 address.
The whale hasn’t fallen for it.
Large holders of Bitcoin, known as whales, move their coins for different reasons, including privacy and safety. Analysts and traders fear that moves like that precede selling as holders feel tempted to realize significant gains.
That said, this is not the first time dormant wallets move their coins. Back in July 2025, an entity moved 80,000 BTC that had sat for 14 years, worth $8.6 billion, the biggest daily movement of coins aged 10 years or more. Ten days later a Satoshi-era wallet sent 40,009 BTC, about $4.7 billion, to Galaxy, which later said it had executed a sale worth roughly $9 billion for a Satoshi-era client.
As of Oct. 13, the original address holds 23,288 sats in leftover dust, about $19, while the five receiving addresses hold the full 4,581.94 BTC.

items.author: Cointelegraph by Sam Bourgi
items.content:
Here’s what happened in crypto today
Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
Today in crypto, Trezor is reducing its authorized reseller network after reports of tampered Ledger wallets, MediaMarktSaturn pulled Ledger products from stores and online platforms and Aptos launched an encrypted transaction feature to protect traders from frontrunning and sandwich attacks.
Trezor cuts reseller network after Ledger wallet tampering reports
Hardware wallet maker Trezor is reducing its authorized reseller network after reports that a Southeast Asian reseller modified Ledger devices to steal users’ recovery phrases.
Trezor said Tuesday the decision was precautionary and that it had no evidence its own devices were compromised. Chief commercial officer Danny Sanders said affected resellers would lose their authorized status on Jan. 1, with shipments to those businesses stopping immediately.
The move follows rival Ledger’s confirmation that at least one device sold by reseller CryptoBilis contained an unauthorized hardware implant capable of capturing recovery phrases and transmitting them over cellular networks.
The incident has raised questions about the security of hardware wallet supply chains. Trezor told Cointelegraph that its existing checks can detect counterfeit devices and modified firmware, but the Ledger implant operated differently by reading information displayed on the device’s screen.
Blockchain investigators have estimated potential losses of between $72 million and $86 million, although Ledger said it had not confirmed the total.
Trezor advised customers to purchase devices directly from the manufacturer and consider multisignature wallets using hardware from different providers.
MediaMarktSaturn pulls Ledger products amid tampering reports
MediaMarktSaturn, the parent company of European electronics retailer MediaMarkt, has removed Ledger products from its physical stores and online platforms amid reports of tampered hardware wallets.
“The products have been removed from our product lineup internationally in all of our countries. We did this as a precautionary measure,” a MediaMarktSaturn spokesperson told Cointelegraph.
Ledger said Tuesday that MediaMarktSaturn suspended sales in coordination with the wallet maker following a report of a hardware implant from a customer in Germany. Ledger said no fund losses had been reported in connection with that case and that it had no indication its infrastructure, systems or services were compromised.
An X user known as Johannes claimed Monday that he purchased two Ledger wallets from separate MediaMarkt stores. He said both contained unauthorized cables and cellular modules.
The security concerns emerged Friday after Ledger said it is investigating reports of losses involving devices sold through Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis. Ledger said Tuesday that implants transmitted users’ recovery phrases over cellular networks and that it was investigating reports beyond CryptoBilis.
Aptos rolls out Encrypted Mempool to curb frontrunning, sandwich attacks
Layer-1 blockchain Aptos has launched an optional new feature that could help shield traders from attacks involving maximal extractable value (MEV), including frontrunning and sandwich attacks.
On Monday, Aptos said its Encrypted Mempool feature is now live on its mainnet, allowing users to opt in to keep pending transactions encrypted until their block ordering is finalized. Aptos said the feature was built for institutions submitting large transactions to the chain, traders wanting to avoid MEV risk, AI agents and builders.
“When you send a transaction on any major chain today, anyone watching the network can see the details before it executes, the function you’re calling, the assets and amounts involved, and the contracts you’re interacting with,” Aptos said. “Bots use that visibility to trade against you or copy your strategy.”
Sandwich attacks, one form of MEV attack, cost Ethereum traders about $60 million over the 12 months through October 2025, according to Cointelegraph’s analysis of EigenPhi data. On Solana, sandwich attacks generated $29.7 million for bots over an 11-month period examined by Bitquery, which identified nearly 6.9 million attacks affecting about 2.2 million wallets.

items.author: Cointelegraph by Turner Wright
items.content:
Trezor reduces resellers as a ‘preventative step’ amid Ledger tampering reports
CCO Danny Sanders said he had notified certain hardware wallet resellers that they would be removed from Trezor’s list of authorized entities starting Jan. 1.
Hardware wallet producer Trezor announced it would reduce its number of resellers as a “preventive step, taken out of an abundance of caution,” following reports that malicious implants had been installed in devices made by competitor Ledger.
In a Tuesday X post, Trezor said there was “not a single piece of evidence that [its] devices have been compromised” after reports that Ledger hardware wallet users had found malicious implants that exposed recovery phrases.
However, Trezor said that it would reduce the number of its resellers, citing “recent supply-chain incidents.” Chief commercial officer Danny Sanders added that he had notified certain resellers that they would be removed from the company’s list of authorized entities on Jan. 1, and would halt shipments of Trezor devices starting on Tuesday.
Source: Trezor CCO Danny Sanders
Trezor’s response came just days after Ledger confirmed that at least one of its devices purchased by a Southeast Asian reseller contained an unauthorized hardware implant, potentially leading to millions of dollars in losses for users. The wallets, sold by reseller CryptoBilis, captured recovery phrases and transmitted them over cellular networks.
“Our setup checks are built to catch counterfeit devices and modified firmware,” a Trezor spokesperson told Cointelegraph. “The implant found in a device bought from CryptoBilis works differently. This is a unique way of tampering with the device, which doesn’t modify the firmware, but reads information on the screen and later sends it to the attacker. So far, we have not seen this specific type of attack on Trezor devices in the real world.”
Related: Ledger investigates fund losses linked to Southeast Asian reseller, warns users
During the investigation, CryptoBilis, an authorized Trezor reseller, suspended all hardware wallet sales. The parent company of European electronics retailer MediaMarkt also announced that it had removed all Ledger products from its physical stores and online platforms “as a precautionary measure.”
How much in user funds was lost?
Blockchain sleuths are still investigating the extent of losses for hardware wallet users, but research from two individuals suggested between $72 million and $86 million. Ledger reported on Tuesday that it had “not confirmed the total number of affected users or the total value lost” due to the breaches.

items.content:
Kalshi and Polymarket won’t be part of FTC sports gambling probe, report
Rival prediction markets Kalshi and Polymarket will reportedly be excluded from the Federal Trade Commission’s (FTC) probe into deceptive practices in the $167 million online sports gambling industry.
The two crypto-linked firms aren’t a focus of the FTC probe, which will instead set its sights on sportsbooks like DraftKings and FanDuel.
It will likely look into misleading advertisements, as well as the rate of suicides, hospitalizations, and bankruptcies caused by the industry.
Sources familiar with the matter told The Washington Sun that the industry evaluation “is in its early stages,” and that it’s conducted by political and career staffers.
New York alleges prediction markets cause problem gambling
Polymarket, which utilises blockchain technology, and Kalshi, which offers crypto perpetuals, are already under the scope of an insider trading probe overseen by Republican House Oversight Committee member James Comer.
The state of New York has also sued Kalshi and Polymarket this year, accusing them both of running an illegal gambling operation that’s encouraging problem gambling among people under the age of 21.
Last month’s Polymarket suit highlighted a study from the National Institutes of Health and American Psychological Association that linked pathological gambling to mental health disorders, suicidal behaviors and substance abuse.
Prediction markets say they aren’t offering gambling
Neither Kalshi nor Polymarket want to be considered gambling, and hope to be regulated federally under the Commodity Futures Trading Commission instead of individual states.
Kalshi CEO Tarek Mansour recently argued that prediction markets aren’t gambling because it is an open financial market that matches buyers and sellers.
Read more: American Indian tribes want Kalshi and Polymarket off their land
Last year, Polymarket CEO Shayne Coplan called DraftKings and FanDuel a sportsbooks “duopoly” that acts against winning bettors.
He said that Polymarket offers derivatives and shouldn’t be regulated like sportsbooks that offer gambling.
President Donald Trump’s son Donald Trump Jr. holds advisory roles in both firms. He holds $300,000 worth of Kalshi shares, and his investment firm 1789 Capital has invested $500 million in Polymarket.

items.content:
In brief
- Strive bought 3,311 BTC worth roughly $280 million between Oct. 5 and Oct. 9 at an average price of about $84,500 per coin, its largest purchase since January, lifting holdings to 32,773 BTC.
- The buy caps an aggressive run—following $169 million and $94.5 million purchases—for the firm, which trades as ASST and recently merged with Semler Scientific to grow its balance sheet.
- It lands amid heavy treasury activity from Strategy, Solana’s DeFi Dev Corp. and Bitmine, as Strive bought into a dip well below Bitcoin’s recent highs.
Strive is piling into Bitcoin at its fastest clip of the year, scooping up another 3,311 BTC worth roughly $280 million in its biggest single purchase since January.
The Nasdaq-listed asset manager, which trades under the ticker ASST, disclosed in a filing Monday that it bought the Bitcoin between Oct. 5 and Oct. 9 at an average price of about $84,500 per coin, including fees. The buy lifts Strive’s total holdings to 32,773 BTC, worth roughly $2.73 billion at today’s prices, up from 29,462 BTC a week earlier.
The purchase caps a stretch of aggressive accumulation. Strive added $169 million in Bitcoin earlier this month in what was then its largest buy in four months, after pushing its stack past 27,000 BTC with a $94.5 million purchase in late September.
The latest tranche extends that momentum, and the timing is notable: the firm bought as Bitcoin slid through a rough week, picking up coins at an average price well below the token’s recent highs near $87,000.
Strive, led by CEO Matthew Cole, is among a wave of public companies that have adopted Bitcoin treasury strategies, raising capital to stockpile the asset and tie their share price to its performance.
The model, pioneered by Michael Saylor’s Strategy, has drawn a crowded field, and Strive has moved aggressively since going public through its merger with Asset Entities, recently completing a tie-up with Semler Scientific to bulk up its balance sheet. Beyond its Bitcoin, the company also holds about 505,000 shares of Strategy’s STRC preferred stock, valued near $50 million, and roughly $310 million in cash.
The buying spree arrives amid a flurry of treasury activity across the sector. Strategy itself recently added $21.5 million in Bitcoin while buying back preferred stock, Solana treasury firm DeFi Development Corp. kept accumulating SOL, and Bitmine continued stacking Ethereum, though chairman Tom Lee said that company is nearly finished and will halt purchases once it holds 5% of the token’s supply.
The strategy carries the category’s familiar risk: Strive’s fortunes rise and fall with a notoriously volatile asset. Buying into a dip can pay off if Bitcoin rebounds, but the same exposure cuts the other way, and treasury firms have faced scrutiny over how much their stock premiums depend on continued accumulation.

items.content:
Broadcom CEO calls AI ‘a casino’ after co-founder dumped $750 million
When Broadcom CEO Hock Tan called AI investors gamblers behaving “like they are in a casino” on Monday, he failed to mention that his company’s own co-founder has sold roughly $750 million worth of AI stock to AI investors this year.
Tan told a Singapore conference on Monday that AI investors are behaving like gamblers who “set very extreme expectations only to find out that it’s almost like they are in a casino.”
He also compared AI spending to arcade tokens, saying, “Your parents give you $10 of tokens, you finish it in 10 minutes and you haven’t learned anything.”
Meanwhile, Broadcom co-founder and director Henry Samueli, who chaired the company’s board of directors until June 2026, spent his year dumping roughly $750 million of stock. If Tan’s casino framing is accurate, Samueli has acted like the house operator raking chips off the table.
Tan spoke this week at the DBS Asia Future Forward Conference, on a panel with Intel’s CEO. According to Bloomberg, he said many AI investors “have no clue what they are investing in.”
Fortunately, many of these ostensibly clueless investors are buying AVGO, Broadcom’s Nasdaq-listed common stock, from his co-founder.
Read more: Credit default swaps forecast AI bankruptcies
Broadcom co-founder Henry Samueli gets rich selling AI stock
Samueli has filed three Form 4s in 2026 worth approximately $250 million apiece.
His March filing covers 781,967 shares sold at a weighted average price of $319.71 apiece. In June, he sold 654,241 shares at $382.13. Lastly, in September, he sold 702,190 shares at $356.04.
In total, he sold 2,138,398 shares for about $750 million.
Tan is also getting rich himself while likening some of his investors to Las Vegas tourists. He personally sold 70,000 shares on January 6 for over $24 million.
As Broadcom insiders got rich, common shareholders have fallen behind their benchmarks.
Broadcom, an AI stock highly dependent on AI capital spending, has trailed the S&P 500 index by 11 percentage points year-to-date, and the Nasdaq 100 index by 18 points.
In its third quarter earnings report, the company admitted that sales of AI semiconductors and infrastructure for AI data centers generated the majority of its total revenue.

items.author: Jose Antonio Lanz
items.content:
In brief
- Palantir CTO Shyam Sankar claimed on CBS that many AI researchers have started smoking to show how much they believe in AI.
- Sankar provide any data, and used the segment to attack effective altruism as a doomsday cult.
- The CDC says smoking causes about one in three U.S. cancer deaths, and Anthropic's Dario Amodei says only actually curing cancer will earn public trust in AI.
Nothing says "I trust the future of medicine" quite like lighting a Marlboro and waiting for the chatbot to fix your lungs. That is the habit Palantir CTO Shyam Sankar says is spreading among AI researchers, who have supposedly started smoking cigarettes to prove how confident they are that AI will cure cancer.
"So many AI researchers have started smoking as a way of signaling to other researchers how much they believe in AI," Sankar said in an interview on CBS News' "Face the Nation" on Sunday. "I believe so much in AI that it's going to cure cancer. So I'm showing you my chips are all in."
He did not name a single researcher, cite a survey, or explain how he knows. The remark landed as an aside while host Margaret Brennan pressed him on why he was so focused on the topic.
He pointed to FTX founder Sam Bankman-Fried as the effective altruist most Americans know, calling the movement a "millenarian doomsday cult." He also invoked Pascal's idea of a god-shaped hole in every human heart, which he suggested some of these researchers are filling with a machine god called AGI.
The medical record is less enthusiastic than the thesis. The CDC says smoking causes roughly one in three cancer deaths in the United States, and cigarette smoke contains at least 69 chemicals known to cause cancer.
Smokers face about 25 times the lung cancer risk of non-smokers, according to the agency. Quitting lowers the risk of 12 types of cancer, and the added lung cancer risk drops by half 10 to 15 years after stopping.
The cancer pitch is not new in this industry. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said in August that promising AI will cure cancer has become “more a cliche than it is inspiring,” and that only actually curing it would earn the public's trust.
2/2 Second, on the messaging around AI. I do not agree that my messaging has been disproportionately negative. In fact it has been about equally balanced between risks and benefits: I’ve written one major essay about each, and even in interviews where I discuss the risks, I…
— Dario Amodei (@DarioAmodei) August 15, 2026
That trust is thin. In the CBS poll Brennan cited, 50% of Americans said AI will create more problems than it solves, 29% said it will solve more than it creates, and 21% were unsure.
About 45% said they want the government to restrict AI's use and development. Smoking to show faith in the technology does not obviously help that number, but it does help AI bros bond with each other. "When you're smoking, you're networking by accident," Revamp AI cofounder Stephen Campbell told Business Insider last month.
The IMF's Kristalina Georgieva recently warned that AI could hit 40% of jobs, and insiders expect a major AI incident within a year. Indirectly causing a lung cancer outbreak was probably not on their bingo card.
Palantir sells data-analysis software to governments and militaries. Most of its business relies on AI.

items.author: Aaron Wise
items.content:
XRPN took shareholder vote with no knowledge of XRP inflation bug
Shareholders of Ripple and Arrington Capital’s XRP treasury stock Evernorth Holdings would have surely loved to know that hackers could have inflated the supply of XRP by trillions of new tokens before they decided last month whether to move forward with a plan to take an XRP crypto treasury company public.
No one told them, while their share redemption window was open prior to September 28, that the XRP Ledger’s base layer payment engine had a bug allowing hackers to mint trillions of new XRP — trading today near $1.35 apiece — for almost nothing.
That bug made the fixed-supply promises of countless XRP proponents, including Evernorth CEO Asheesh Birla’s claim that 100 billion XRP was a ceiling that would never move, unenforceable on the network itself.
“All 100 billion XRP tokens were created at the time of the XRP Ledger’s launch in 2012,” Evernorth’s proxy filing read. In fact, hackers could have minted orders of magnitude more over the past decade.
Read more: Ripple pushes urgent XRPL patch — but nodes must trust its new key
Voting in an information vacuum about XRP
Although validators on the XRP Ledger have patched the bug, its existence amid Evernorth’s shareholder redemption offer is remarkable.
According to the official story, unbeknownst to XRPN shareholders — and almost everybody else on the planet — an ethical researcher privately reported the bug to Ripple’s developer arm on September 22.
Ripple then shipped an emergency, closed-source fix on September 25, obscuring that release in veiled language about “integer-arithmetic hardening.”
Shareholders faced a September 28 redemption deadline to redeem XRPN shares for cash and/or back out of the plan to merge Evernorth, an XRP treasury stock whose core value proposition rests on XRP’s limited supply, onto public markets.
The vote to proceed onto Nasdaq passed on September 30, and the merger closed on October 9.
Only on that date, October 9, did an official report admit what the September 25 “integer-arithmetic hardening” patch actually fixed: a catastrophic inflation bug that could have sent the price of XRP to near-$0.
Fortunately, the network got lucky and no one actually exploited the vulnerability while it was active.
Still, XRPN shareholders made irreversible decisions within that time window.
‘That number will never change’
Birla, a former Ripple executive and the CEO of XRPN, said on the SPAC Insider podcast, in a transcript Evernorth filed with the SEC, that “XRP is a pre-mined digital asset. One hundred billion XRP were created at inception, and that number will never change. A significant portion is held in escrow by Ripple.”
Although that number has technically never changed, it certainly could have if another researcher had utilized that inflation bug.
The flaw, per the official report, likely went back to 2015.
Researcher Cayden Liao and Veria AI reported the “overflow” issue, a euphemism for an inflation bug, on September 22 through a bug bounty program.
RippleX and the XRP Ledger Foundation reproduced the exploit, escalated its severity rating to critical, and paid the bounty.
The patch shipped September 25 in xrpld 3.4.1, with no amendment vote.
XRPN pitched XRP’s capped supply that almost wasn’t
The bug report states that a single validated transaction using the exploit “could have created spendable XRP far beyond the total supply.”
Ripple Labs is an investor in and named counterparty to the business combination agreement that took Evernorth public.
Evernorth’s registration statement carried generic boilerplate. It said the cryptography underlying the XRP Ledger could “be flawed or ineffective,” per the prospectus shareholders received.
Nothing disclosed, while the XRPN redemption window was open prior to September 30 vote, that the XRP supply cap was technically meaningless for most of the XRP Ledger’s existence.
